name: Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarship – Embassy Recommendation
provider: Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology (MEXT), Government of Japan
fields: any (Research Students in any field; Undergraduate all majors; College of Technology (KOSEN) and Specialized Training College technical/vocational fields; Japanese Studies, Teacher Training and Young Leaders' Program tracks)
eligibility: Cambodian citizen; Research students: under 35, university graduate with good grades; Undergraduate/KOSEN/Specialized Training: aged 17–24 with 12 years of schooling; Teacher Training: under 35 with 5+ years teaching; Young Leaders' Program: under 40 civil servant/professional; good health
cambodia_note: Apply to the Embassy of Japan in Phnom Penh (Scholarship Office, scholarship.jpn@pp.mofa.go.jp, tel 023-217-161). The embassy runs the first screening (document check, written exams in English/Japanese/maths/science, interview) around May–July, then recommends candidates to MEXT for the second screening.
deadline_note: Embassy recruits each April–May for arrival in Japan the following April or September/October (the 2027 cycle was recruited April–May 2026 and is closed; the 2028 cycle should open around April 2027); first screening May–July; final results around January
language_req: English or Japanese (embassy exams in English and Japanese; no fixed test score; Japanese language course provided)
verdict: Search results confirm the official page 'MEXT Scholarship 2027 | Embassy of Japan in Cambodia' at the given URL listing Research, Undergraduate, KOSEN, Specialized Training, Japanese Studies, Teacher Training and YLP categories, and the Study in Japan 2027 guidelines confirm April–May recruitment with May–July embassy screening and JPY 117,000/143,000/145,000 stipends; the page itself could not be fetched (egress blocked).
changes: deadline_note clarified that the 2027 cycle closed in May 2026 and the next window is around April–May 2027; added the official 2027 research guidelines PDF to source_urls; confidence lowered slightly because pages were verified only via search snippets

name: Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarship – University Recommendation
provider: Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology (MEXT), Government of Japan
fields: any (mostly graduate research/degree programmes; some undergraduate, Japanese studies and KOSEN places)
eligibility: Nationals of countries with diplomatic relations with Japan (Cambodia included); research/graduate applicants under 35 with a university degree; must be admitted to a MEXT-approved Japanese university that nominates them; good health
cambodia_note: No embassy step: Cambodians apply directly to a Japanese university's graduate school/international office (ask for 'MEXT scholarship by university recommendation'); the university screens and nominates to MEXT. Contact a professor or lab 6–12 months before the university deadline.
deadline_note: Deadlines set by each university, commonly October–January (some to spring) for arrival the following September/October (some April); e.g. Hokkaido University expects AY2027 general-category documents by 22 January 2027
language_req: English or Japanese depending on the programme; test scores per university
verdict: Search results from the official Study in Japan page and university pages (Hokkaido University AY2027, University of Tokyo, Kyoto University) confirm the university-recommendation track runs for AY2027 with each university screening and nominating candidates, deadlines around late December to January 2027; pages could not be fetched directly.
changes: added a Hokkaido University AY2027 deadline example to deadline_note and university source pages; cambodia_note adds the advice to contact a professor early; otherwise none

name: Global Korea Scholarship for Graduate Degrees (GKS-G) – Embassy Track
provider: National Institute for International Education (NIIED), Ministry of Education, Republic of Korea
fields: any (Type A and Type B universities; regional R-GKS track)
covers: thesis printing and degree completion grants
eligibility: Cambodian citizen (applicant and parents must not hold Korean citizenship); under 40 on 1 September of the intake year; bachelor's or master's degree completed by 31 August; cumulative GPA at least 80% or 2.64/4.0; good health; prior GKS-G recipients generally ineligible
cambodia_note: Apply online via Study in Korea choosing the Embassy of the Republic of Korea in Cambodia; Cambodia had 12 embassy-track places in 2026. Embassy document screening and interview, then university screening; results around June; arrival late August. The embassy also announces a separate AKS Graduate School of Korean Studies GKS track (5 places for Cambodia in 2026).
deadline_note: Embassy track opens mid-February and closes late February each year (2026: 12–25 February, 4pm Phnom Penh time); the 2027 call is expected in February 2027; university track follows in March
language_req: none required; TOPIK or English (IELTS/TOEFL) scores earn bonus points; 1-year Korean course before the degree unless TOPIK 5+
verdict: Search results confirm the 2026 GKS-G call (2,000 scholars, Cambodia 12 embassy-track places, 12–25 February 2026 window) from the Study in Korea notice board and Khmer Times, plus the embassy's 2026 AKS track notice (5 places); the KRW 1,000,000 monthly graduate stipend is confirmed by NIIED guideline summaries; embassy and Study in Korea pages could not be fetched directly.
changes: apply_url changed from the embassy's 2025 GKS-G notice (seq=38, which search results title '2025 GKS Program for Graduate Degrees') to the embassy announcements board where each year's call is posted; deadline_note notes the next call is expected February 2027; added the Study in Korea 2026 GKS-G notice to source_urls

name: Global Korea Scholarship for Undergraduate Degrees (GKS-U) – Embassy Track
provider: National Institute for International Education (NIIED), Ministry of Education, Republic of Korea
fields: any (bachelor's at Type A/B universities; associate degrees via university track)
eligibility: Cambodian citizen (applicant and parents non-Korean); under 25 (born after 1 March 2002 for the 2027 cycle); completed or completing 12 years of schooling by February 2027; GPA at least 80% or 2.64/4.0 (top 20%); no previous degree in Korea; good health
cambodia_note: Apply online via Study in Korea selecting the Korean Embassy in Phnom Penh (the 2026 round required offline submission to the embassy because of a system outage, so watch the embassy notice board). Embassy shortlists and interviews, then NIIED and university screening; results announced in January; arrival late February. General-track applicants list up to 3 universities including at least one Type B.
deadline_note: Opens mid-September and closes 30 September each year (2027 cycle: 15–30 September 2026, 6pm KST); university track opens in October
language_req: none required; TOPIK/English scores give bonus points; 1-year Korean course before the degree
verdict: Multiple 2027 GKS-U guides and Korea JoongAng Daily confirm the 2027 embassy-track window of 15–30 September 2026 (18:00 KST) with results January 2027 and arrival late February 2027; the Korean Embassy in Cambodia's 2026 GKS-U notices (seq=66, seq=71) appear in search results, but no 2027 Cambodia-specific notice was found and the embassy site could not be fetched.
changes: cambodia_note softened 'results announced 7 January' to 'in January' since that date belonged to the 2026 cycle; apply_url still points to the embassy's 2026 notice because the 2027 embassy notice could not be located; otherwise none

name: Chinese Government Scholarship – Bilateral Program (Type A, via embassy/MoEYS)
provider: China Scholarship Council (CSC), Ministry of Education of the People's Republic of China
fields: any (undergraduate, master's, doctoral, general scholar and senior scholar programmes at CSC-designated universities)
covers: monthly stipend (CNY 2,500 bachelor, 3,000 master/general scholar, 3,500 PhD/senior scholar)
eligibility: Non-Chinese citizen in good health; bachelor: high-school graduate under 25 (must take the CSCA test); master: bachelor's degree, under 35; PhD: master's degree, under 40; general scholar under 45; HSK 3–4 for Chinese-taught programmes; cannot hold another Chinese government scholarship
cambodia_note: Type A: Cambodians apply through the Chinese Embassy in Phnom Penh together with Cambodia's Ministry of Education, Youth and Sport (MoEYS), which publishes the annual call and runs a selection exam; the online application on campuschina.org uses the embassy's agency number and a pre-admission letter from a Chinese university is required. Cambodia receives several dozen bilateral places each year (about 2,700 Cambodians funded to date).
deadline_note: Online application on campuschina.org opens each autumn/winter; embassy deadlines fall roughly January–April (many embassies closed 2026/27 applications around 8 February 2026); bachelor applicants must sit the CSCA in December or January; MoEYS selection in spring; results around July for September entry

summary_en: Full scholarship for Cambodian students aged roughly 14-16 to study four years in Singapore from Secondary 3 through A-Level, with no service bond.
eligibility_km: សញ្ជាតិខ្មែរ កើតក្នុងឆ្នាំដែលកំណត់ក្នុងការប្រកាសនីមួយៗ មានលទ្ធផលសិក្សាល្អជាប់លាប់ និងចេះភាសាអង់គ្លេសល្អ
covers_km: ថ្លៃសិក្សា ប្រាក់ឧបត្ថម្ភប្រចាំឆ្នាំ កន្លែងស្នាក់នៅ សំបុត្រយន្តហោះ និងថ្លៃប្រឡង O-Level និង A-Level
deadline_km: ជាធម្មតាបើកទទួលពាក្យខែមេសា ដល់ខែឧសភា
fields_km: ថ្នាក់វិទ្យាល័យទូទៅ (O-Level និង A-Level)
cambodia_km: ដាក់ពាក្យតាមអនឡាញនៅទំព័រសម្រាប់កម្ពុជាលើគេហទំព័រ MOE សិង្ហបុរី។ បេក្ខជនដែលជាប់វគ្គដំបូងនឹងត្រូវអញ្ជើញមកប្រឡង និងសម្ភាសនៅភ្នំពេញ។
language_km: អង់គ្លេស (ប្រឡងអង់គ្លេស និងគណិតវិទ្យា)

name: Singapore Cooperation Programme (SCP) Training Courses
provider: Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Singapore
fields: Short courses for officials in public administration, economic development, urban planning, education, health, ICT, aviation and more
eligibility: Government officials of developing partner countries (Cambodia is a long-standing partner) nominated by their agency; relevant job role; working English
cambodia_note: Cambodian officials are nominated through their ministries and the Cambodia-Singapore Cooperation Centre (CSCC) in Phnom Penh; the Singapore Embassy in Phnom Penh coordinates; over 17,700 Cambodian officials have trained under SCP.
deadline_note: Rolling; each course on the SCP calendar has its own nomination deadline

name: ICCR Scholarships (General Scholarship Scheme and Mekong-Ganga Cooperation Scholarship Scheme)
provider: Indian Council for Cultural Relations (ICCR), Ministry of External Affairs, Government of India
fields: Most fields except medicine/dentistry (engineering, IT, humanities, social sciences, business, agriculture, Buddhist studies, forensic science, arts, yoga)
covers: monthly stipend (approx. INR 18,000 UG / 20,000 PG / 22,000 PhD)
eligibility: Cambodian citizens aged 18–30 for undergraduate/postgraduate under the general scheme (up to 40 under the Mekong-Ganga scheme, higher for PhD); completed secondary school or bachelor's with good marks; English proficiency; medical fitness
cambodia_note: Apply online on the ICCR A2A portal selecting the Embassy of India, Phnom Penh; the embassy Education Wing (edu.phnompenh@mea.gov.in, +855 23 210 912) screens candidates and administers an English test; Cambodia also has dedicated Mekong-Ganga Cooperation places; 41 Cambodians were selected for 2026–27.
deadline_note: Opens around February and closes mid-April each year (2026–27: 15 April 2026); classes begin July–August
language_req: English proficiency (embassy-administered test; some institutions ask for TOEFL/IELTS)

name: Indian Technical and Economic Cooperation (ITEC) Programme
provider: Ministry of External Affairs, Government of India
fields: About 400 short professional courses (IT, management, public administration, finance, agriculture, renewable energy, English, defence etc.) at 100+ Indian institutes
eligibility: Working professionals and government officials of ITEC partner countries (Cambodia included), aged 25–45, at least 5 years' work experience, working knowledge of English, nominated/endorsed by employer
cambodia_note: Apply online at itecgoi.in choosing the Embassy of India, Phnom Penh; the embassy vets applications and forwards them to MEA; the embassy holds ITEC briefings for Cambodian officials.
deadline_note: Year-round; apply at least about 3 months before the course starts (course calendar runs April–March)

name: Government of Brunei Darussalam Scholarship to Foreign Students (BDGS)
provider: Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Brunei Darussalam
fields: Diploma, undergraduate and master's programmes at UBD, UNISSA, UTB, KUPU SB and Politeknik Brunei
covers: accommodation at the institution's residential college
one return economy air ticket and baggage allowance
eligibility: Citizens of ASEAN, Commonwealth, OIC and other countries (not Brunei permanent residents); studying in Brunei for the first time; not above 25 for diploma/undergraduate and 35 for master's on 1 July of the start year; meets institution's entry requirements; English proficiency (IELTS 6.0/TOEFL 550 for English-medium)
cambodia_note: Cambodia is eligible as an ASEAN member; apply online on the MFA Brunei BDGS portal within the window; awardees are confirmed through the Brunei Embassy in Phnom Penh/Cambodian authorities.
deadline_note: Opens around December–January and closes mid-February (2026/27: 15 February 2026); academic year starts July/August
language_req: IELTS 6.0 / TOEFL 550 or equivalent for English-medium programmes

name: Malaysian Technical Cooperation Programme (MTCP) Scholarship
provider: Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Malaysia
fields: Most fields at Malaysian public universities, except medicine, nursing and clinical pharmacy
eligibility: Citizens of MTCP recipient countries (Cambodia included); not more than 45 at application; Second Class Upper or minimum CGPA 3.0–3.5 at bachelor level (per current guidelines); IELTS 6.0 / TOEFL iBT 60 or English-medium degree; not concurrently on another scholarship; full-time master's at an approved Malaysian university
cambodia_note: Apply online on the MTCP scholarship portal; no embassy nomination required, though the Malaysian Embassy in Phnom Penh may verify documents.
deadline_note: Opens around April and closes in June (2026: 12 June 2026) for the September/October intake
language_req: IELTS 6.0 or TOEFL iBT 60 (or English-medium prior degree)

name: Malaysia International Scholarship (MIS)
provider: Ministry of Higher Education, Malaysia
fields: Priority areas: science and engineering, agriculture and fisheries, economics and Islamic finance, ICT, biotechnology, biosecurity and food safety, infrastructure and utility, environmental studies, health sciences (not medicine, nursing, pharmacy)
eligibility: International students (Cambodians eligible); not above 40 for master's / 45 for PhD; CGPA 3.5 or equivalent; IELTS 6.5 or TOEFL iBT 92 (or equivalent); admission offer from a Malaysian university
cambodia_note: Open to all nationalities including Cambodian; apply online on the MOHE biasiswa portal; no embassy step.
deadline_note: Opens early March and closes early April (2026/27: 4 March–3 April 2026); shortlisted applicants interviewed afterwards

name: KNB Scholarship (Kemitraan Negara Berkembang / Developing Countries Partnership)
provider: Ministry of Higher Education, Science and Technology (Kemdiktisaintek), Republic of Indonesia
fields: any of about 1,170 study programmes at 47 Indonesian universities
eligibility: Citizens of developing countries with diplomatic relations with Indonesia (Cambodia eligible); maximum age 21 for bachelor's, 35 for master's, 40 for doctoral; required prior qualification; IELTS 5.5 / TOEFL iBT 53 (bachelor) or IELTS 6.0 / TOEFL iBT 61–71 (master/PhD) unless English-medium degree; recommendation letter from the Indonesian Embassy
cambodia_note: Obtain a recommendation letter from the Indonesian Embassy in Phnom Penh (submit passport, certificates, transcripts and university invitation letter), then apply online on the KNB portal.
deadline_note: Opens early February and closes end of March (2026: 2 February–31 March 2026); results mid-June; departure August
language_req: IELTS 5.5 (bachelor) or 6.0 (master/PhD) / TOEFL equivalents; Indonesian language year provided

name: Darmasiswa Indonesian Scholarship
provider: Ministry of Primary and Secondary Education, Republic of Indonesia (with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs)
fields: One-year non-degree study of Indonesian language, arts and culture at about 54 universities
eligibility: Foreign nationals from countries with diplomatic relations with Indonesia (Cambodia included); aged about 18–32 (window set each cycle); completed secondary education; able to communicate in English; good health; not a Darmasiswa/KNB alumnus or currently studying/working in Indonesia
cambodia_note: Cambodians apply online on the Darmasiswa portal; the Indonesian Embassy in Phnom Penh interviews and endorses shortlisted applicants.
deadline_note: Registration usually in the first half of the year (2026/27: 15 May–15 June 2026); programme starts late August/September
language_req: basic English; courses taught in Indonesian

name: Hong Kong PhD Fellowship Scheme (HKPFS)
provider: Research Grants Council (RGC), Hong Kong SAR Government
fields: any (full-time PhD at the eight UGC-funded universities)
covers: conference and research travel allowance HK$14,400 per year
support for up to 3 years (universities usually add tuition waivers/extra support)
eligibility: New applicants to full-time PhD programmes at UGC-funded Hong Kong universities, any nationality; outstanding academic performance, research potential, communication and leadership
cambodia_note: No country quota; Cambodians submit an initial application on the RGC HKPFS online system and full applications to up to two chosen universities by their own deadlines.
deadline_note: Opens 1 September; initial application closes 1 December (12:00 noon HKT) each year for entry the following September (400 fellowships for 2027/28)

name: Macao Foundation Belt and Road Scholarship
provider: Macao Foundation (Macao SAR Government)
fields: any full-time programme at Macao higher-education institutions (University of Macau, MUST, Macao Polytechnic University, City University of Macau etc.)
covers: annual scholarship of MOP 60,000–80,000 towards tuition and living costs
eligibility: Students from Bangladesh, Brazil, Cambodia, Hungary, Indonesia, Malaysia, Mongolia, Philippines, Portugal, Thailand or Vietnam, recommended by their home ministry of education or a PRC diplomatic post, and accepted and recommended by a Macao higher-education institution; about 20 places per year
cambodia_note: Cambodia is named; obtain a recommendation from Cambodia's Ministry of Education, Youth and Sport (or via the Chinese Embassy in Phnom Penh) and apply through the Macao university's international office.
deadline_note: Through the universities' admission cycles, generally spring for August entry

name: Kazakhstan Government Scholarship for Foreign Citizens
provider: Ministry of Science and Higher Education of the Republic of Kazakhstan, administered by the Center for International Programs
fields: any at 27 participating Kazakh universities (550 grants: 490 bachelor, 50 master, 10 PhD)
eligibility: Foreign citizens of any country (Cambodians eligible), including ethnic Kazakhs without Kazakh citizenship; completed secondary/bachelor's/master's education; language of instruction Kazakh, Russian or English per programme
cambodia_note: No embassy step; apply online at studyin.kz/admission during the annual window.
deadline_note: Online window roughly late March to 31 May (2026: closed 31 May 2026); results in summer for September entry
language_req: Kazakh, Russian or English depending on programme

name: SEARCA Graduate Scholarship (Master's and PhD)
provider: SEAMEO Southeast Asian Regional Center for Graduate Study and Research in Agriculture (SEARCA), hosted by the Philippines
host_country: Various (Philippines, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia partner universities)
fields: Agriculture and related sciences (agri-food systems, rural development, natural resources, agricultural economics)
eligibility: Nationals of SEAMEO member countries (Cambodia included); typically under 35 (MS) / under 40 (PhD); employed by a university, government agency or research institution in the home country; strong academic record; English proficiency
cambodia_note: Cambodians apply online through SEARCA's iSCHO portal with endorsement from their employer/ministry (e.g. Ministry of Agriculture or MoEYS); no embassy step.
deadline_note: Call opens around June–July with deadline 30 September for the following academic year (AY2026–27 closed 30 September 2025)

name: JDS – Project for Human Resource Development Scholarship (Cambodia)
provider: Government of Japan (JICA grant aid), implemented by JICE
fields: Development-related English-taught programmes (public policy, economics, law, engineering, agriculture, education, ICT, health, environment)
eligibility: Cambodian nationals aged about 22–39 (master's), university graduates working in the Cambodian government or designated organizations with around 2+ years' experience; doctoral track for officials/JDS alumni (older age cap); English-taught study
cambodia_note: Cambodia-specific programme managed by the JICE JDS Project Office in Phnom Penh; apply via the JDS Cambodia page, with document screening, English test and interviews; about 20–25 places a year.
deadline_note: Call opens around September–October with deadline in late November (2026 intake: 28 November 2025, 3pm); results around March; departure August/September

name: KOICA Scholarship Program (Master's and Doctoral)
provider: Korea International Cooperation Agency (KOICA), Government of the Republic of Korea
fields: Development-related programmes (public policy, economic development, ICT, health, engineering, agriculture, education) at partner Korean universities
eligibility: Government officials and public-sector employees of KOICA partner countries (Cambodia included), usually under 40 (master's) / 45 (doctoral), bachelor's degree, nominated by their ministry; English proficiency; not previously KOICA degree scholars
cambodia_note: Apply through the KOICA Cambodia Office in Phnom Penh with nomination from the employing ministry/Cambodian government; programme-specific information sheets are issued with the annual guideline.
deadline_note: Guideline published around June; applications close June–July (2027 programme: 29 June 2026, 4pm); study begins the following August/September
language_req: English (TOEFL/IELTS may be required by the host university)

name: Australia Awards Scholarships (Cambodia)
provider: Australian Government, Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT)
fields: All fields relevant to Cambodia's development (climate-related study strongly encouraged); general management degrees such as MBA are not funded
covers: pre-departure English language training in Cambodia
eligibility: Cambodian citizen resident in Cambodia for the 24 months before the closing date; bachelor degree; at least 24 months of relevant full-time work experience at closing date; IELTS 6.5 overall with no band below 6.0 (or equivalent) at application; not an Australian citizen/permanent resident; women, people with disability and applicants from provinces encouraged
cambodia_note: Cambodia is a priority country with its own Australia Awards Cambodia office in Phnom Penh. Apply online through DFAT's OASIS portal; the 2027 intake also allocated Mekong-Australia Partnership (AA-MAP) places to Cambodians under the same application.
deadline_note: Opens 1 February and closes 30 April (14:00 AEST) each year; the 2027 intake ran 1 February–30 April 2026, and the 2028 intake is expected to open February 2027
language_req: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent TOEFL iBT/PTE) at time of application

name: Australia Awards Mekong-Australia Partnership Scholarships (AA-MAP)
provider: Australian Government DFAT – Mekong-Australia Partnership
fields: Water security, climate action, gender equality/disability equity and social inclusion (GEDSI), combatting transnational crime, economic resilience and subregional integration
eligibility: Citizens of Cambodia, Laos, Myanmar, Thailand or Vietnam meeting the standard Australia Awards criteria (bachelor degree, minimum work experience, IELTS 6.5 no band below 6.0, residency in home country); Master's by coursework or research in the MAP thematic areas
cambodia_note: 30 AA-MAP scholarships across the Mekong subregion with 5 allocated to Cambodian citizens; Cambodians apply through the same OASIS application and Australia Awards Cambodia process as the main Australia Awards intake.
deadline_note: Same window as Australia Awards: opens 1 February and closes 30 April each year (2027 intake closed 30 April 2026); 2028 intake expected February–April 2027
language_req: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent)

name: Manaaki New Zealand Scholarships
provider: New Zealand Government – Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade (New Zealand Aid Programme)
fields: Postgraduate study in subjects that contribute to Cambodia's development (e.g., agriculture, climate and renewable energy, disaster risk management, public sector management, education, health)
covers: home leave/reunion travel for long programmes
up to one year of English language training in Cambodia for preferred candidates
eligibility: Cambodian citizen aged 18+, resident in Cambodia for at least 2 years before applying; at least 1 year full-time (or 2 years part-time) work experience; must not hold NZ/Australian citizenship or residence; must return to Cambodia for at least 2 years after study; Cambodians may only study at postgraduate level (Postgraduate Diploma, Master's, PhD)
cambodia_note: Cambodia is an eligible Asian country (postgraduate only). Apply online at nzscholarships.govt.nz; the Manaaki New Zealand Scholarships Office in Cambodia is hosted by IDP Education at the ACE Tuol Tom Poung campus, Phnom Penh.
deadline_note: One selection round per year, usually opening in February/March and closing in March; the 2026 round (for study from 2027) opened 1 March 2026 and closed 31 March (extended to 10 April) 2026; the next round is expected in February–March 2027
language_req: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent for postgraduate entry; English language training pathway available for Cambodian candidates

name: Chevening Scholarships
provider: UK Government – Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office
fields: Any one-year taught master's degree at a UK university
covers: return economy airfare to the UK
travel grant to attend Chevening events in the UK
eligibility: Cambodian citizen who will return to Cambodia for at least 2 years after the award; completed undergraduate degree enabling entry to a UK postgraduate programme; at least 2 years (2,800 hours) of work experience; apply to three eligible UK master's courses and hold an unconditional offer from one by 8 July 2027; not previously funded by a UK government scholarship
cambodia_note: Cambodia has its own Chevening country page and allocation; applications are made through the Chevening online application system and interviews are held with the British Embassy in Phnom Penh.
deadline_note: Opens in early August and closes in early October each year; 2027/2028 applications close 6 October 2026 at 11:00 UTC
language_req: No English test required at application; must meet the chosen UK university's English requirement (typically IELTS 6.5) for an unconditional offer

name: Fulbright Foreign Student Program (Cambodia)
provider: U.S. Department of State – administered by the U.S. Embassy Phnom Penh, Public Diplomacy Section
fields: Most academic fields (clinical medicine and programmes requiring patient contact excluded)
covers: round-trip airfare to the United States
eligibility: Cambodian citizen residing in Cambodia at time of application; bachelor's degree (for master's study) or master's degree (for doctoral study) with a strong academic record; minimum TOEFL iBT 88 / TOEFL ITP 570 / IELTS 7.0; relevant work experience preferred; not a U.S. citizen or permanent resident
cambodia_note: Cambodians apply directly through the U.S. Embassy Phnom Penh, which runs its own annual competition and online application; the 2027-2028 competition closed on 30 April 2026 (23:59 ET).
deadline_note: Announced around February and closes 30 April each year; the 2027-2028 cycle closed 30 April 2026 and the 2028-2029 cycle is expected to open around February 2027
language_req: TOEFL iBT 88 or IELTS 7.0 (or TOEFL ITP 570) minimum

name: Hubert H. Humphrey Fellowship Program
provider: U.S. Department of State (Fulbright program) – via U.S. Embassy Phnom Penh
fields: Public policy-related fields: sustainable development, democratic institution building, education, public health, journalism, law and human rights, technology policy, etc.
eligibility: Young or mid-career professionals with a completed undergraduate degree, at least five years of substantial full-time professional experience, demonstrated leadership and public-service commitment, limited or no prior experience in the United States, and English proficiency (TOEFL required for finalists). Ten-month non-degree program.
cambodia_note: Cambodian candidates apply directly to the Public Diplomacy Section of the U.S. Embassy in Phnom Penh, which recruits and nominates Cambodian applicants each year. The 2027-2028 call closed on 19 July 2026 (23:59 Cambodia time); the next call (for 2028-2029) is expected in mid-2027.
deadline_note: Announced in the second quarter each year; 2027-2028 cycle closed 19 July 2026. Next call expected around May-July 2027.
language_req: English proficiency required; TOEFL (typically iBT 71+) or IELTS 6.0 for finalists

name: Global Undergraduate Exchange Program (Global UGRAD)
provider: U.S. Department of State, Bureau of Educational and Cultural Affairs – administered by World Learning
fields: Any field (one semester of non-degree undergraduate study plus community service and professional development)
eligibility: Cambodian citizen aged 18+ currently enrolled full-time in an undergraduate degree in Cambodia, having completed at least the first semester and with at least one full academic year remaining after the programme; demonstrated leadership; minimum TOEFL iBT 48 for finalists; not a U.S. citizen/permanent resident
cambodia_note: Cambodia is an eligible country; applications are submitted through the World Learning online portal and screened by the U.S. Embassy Phnom Penh Public Affairs Section (PASExchanges@state.gov). The 2026-27 application has closed and the 2027-28 cycle had not yet been announced at time of research; confirm status with the embassy.
deadline_note: Historically opens in November/December and closes in January/February for the following academic year; 2027-28 dates not yet published
language_req: TOEFL iBT 48 minimum (finalists); good written and spoken English

name: DAAD Development-Related Postgraduate Courses (EPOS)
provider: DAAD – German Academic Exchange Service, funded by the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ)
fields: Development-related postgraduate courses: economics/business, development cooperation, engineering, mathematics, regional and urban planning, agriculture and forestry, natural and environmental sciences, medicine and public health, social sciences, education, law, media
covers: monthly payment of EUR 992 (postgraduate) or EUR 1,400 (doctoral)
health, accident and personal liability insurance
tuition-free study or fee coverage at the selected course
rent subsidy and family allowances where applicable
eligibility: Nationals of developing countries on the DAAD list (Cambodia included); bachelor degree (usually four-year) in an appropriate subject normally not older than six years; at least two years of relevant professional experience after the first degree; willingness to return and contribute to home-country development; language proficiency required by the course
cambodia_note: Cambodia is on the EPOS eligible country list. There is no embassy nomination: applicants apply directly to the German university course of their choice, which forwards its shortlist to DAAD.
deadline_note: Deadlines are set by each course; most fall between August and October 2026 (some until December) for courses starting in 2027/2028 — see the DAAD EPOS deadline list
language_req: English (typically IELTS 6.0 / TOEFL iBT 80+) or German depending on the course

name: DAAD Research Grants – Doctoral Programmes in Germany (CLMTV / Cambodia)
provider: DAAD – German Academic Exchange Service (funded by the German Federal Foreign Office)
fields: Any academic discipline
covers: monthly stipend of EUR 1,400 for doctoral candidates
health, accident and personal liability insurance
rent subsidy and family allowances where applicable
eligibility: Excellent master's degree (normally not older than six years) and a research proposal agreed with a supervising professor at a German university or research institute; for full doctoral programmes funding of up to 4 years; short-term research grants (2–12 months) for candidates doing a doctorate at home; language proficiency required by the host
cambodia_note: Cambodian applicants are covered by the DAAD Regional Office Hanoi (CLMTV: Cambodia, Laos, Myanmar, Thailand, Vietnam); applications go through the DAAD portal with the CLMTV deadlines — Doctoral Programmes in Germany and bi-nationally supervised doctorates 21 October 2026, short-term Research Grants 7 October 2026 (for funding starting 2027).
deadline_note: Annual call; for Cambodia the deadline is in October (21 October 2026 for doctoral programmes starting 2027; 7 October 2026 for short-term research grants)
language_req: English or German proficiency as required by the host institution

name: Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters Scholarships
provider: European Union – Erasmus+ programme (European Education and Culture Executive Agency)
fields: Any field – each of the 200+ joint master programmes covers its own discipline; study takes place in at least two European countries
covers: participation costs including tuition, library/lab fees and full insurance
monthly living allowance of EUR 1,400 for up to 24 months
contribution to travel and installation costs
eligibility: Bachelor degree (or equivalent) meeting the consortium's admission criteria; open to students of any nationality worldwide; a student may receive only one Erasmus Mundus scholarship; each consortium sets its own academic and language requirements
cambodia_note: Cambodian nationals apply directly to the joint master consortium of their choice via the programme's own website; no embassy or ministry nomination is involved. Non-EU applicants are ranked in the worldwide scholarship competition.
deadline_note: Each programme sets its own deadline; most applications for September 2027 entry must be submitted between October 2026 and January/February 2027
language_req: English (typically IELTS 6.5 / TOEFL iBT 90) or the programme's teaching language

name: Swiss Government Excellence Scholarships (ESKAS) – Research Fellowship and PhD
provider: Swiss Confederation – Federal Commission for Scholarships for Foreign Students (FCS/ESKAS), State Secretariat for Education, Research and Innovation (SERI)
fields: Any discipline (research at doctoral level at a Swiss public university, ETH or research institute)
covers: tuition fee waiver at most host universities
return airfare at the end of the scholarship for nationals of eligible countries
eligibility: Master's degree (or equivalent) obtained before the scholarship start; born after 31 December 1991 (under 35); letter of support from an academic supervisor at a Swiss university is mandatory; applicants must not have stayed in Switzerland for more than one year at the start; postdoctoral scholarships are no longer awarded from 2027/28
cambodia_note: Cambodia is on the ESKAS country list for the Research Fellowship and PhD scholarship types; Cambodian candidates apply through the ESKAS online portal and the Embassy of Switzerland in Bangkok (bangkok@eda.admin.ch), which handles Cambodia. The 2027-2028 call for Cambodia opened 1 September 2026 and closes 24 November 2026.
deadline_note: Opens 1 September and closes late November each year (2027-2028 cycle for Cambodia: 1 September – 24 November 2026)
language_req: Sufficient English (or French/German/Italian) as required by the Swiss supervisor; no fixed test score

name: Stipendium Hungaricum Scholarship Programme
provider: Government of Hungary – Tempus Public Foundation
fields: Any field for Cambodian applicants, primarily agriculture, engineering, economics, natural sciences, social sciences, computer science and IT (bachelor, master, one-tier master, PhD and preparatory programmes)
covers: monthly stipend of HUF 43,700 (bachelor/master) or HUF 140,000–180,000 (PhD)
free dormitory place or HUF 40,000 monthly housing contribution
Hungarian public health insurance plus supplementary medical insurance
eligibility: Cambodian citizen aged 18 or over by 31 August of the intake year; secondary school certificate (bachelor), bachelor degree (master) or master degree (PhD); must meet the host university's programme and language requirements; nominated by Cambodia's sending partner ministry
cambodia_note: Cambodia is a Stipendium Hungaricum partner country with roughly 30 places per year. Apply online at apply.stipendiumhungaricum.hu and submit the required documents to the Ministry of Education, Youth and Sport (MoEYS), which nominates candidates to Tempus Public Foundation.
deadline_note: Opens in mid-November and closes 15 January (14:00 CET) each year; the 2027/2028 call opens in November 2026 with a deadline expected around 15 January 2027
language_req: English (typically B2 / IELTS 5.5–6.5 depending on university) or Hungarian for Hungarian-taught programmes

name: Türkiye Scholarships (Türkiye Bursları)
provider: Government of the Republic of Türkiye – Presidency for Turks Abroad and Related Communities (YTB)
fields: Any field at Turkish state universities (associate, undergraduate, master's and doctoral programmes)
covers: monthly stipend of TL 4,500 (associate/bachelor), TL 6,500 (master) or TL 9,000 (PhD)
eligibility: Not a Turkish citizen; under 21 for undergraduate, under 30 for master's and under 35 for PhD applicants; minimum academic average of 70% (undergraduate), 75% (graduate) or 90% (health sciences); graduates of or current students at Turkish universities are not eligible
cambodia_note: Open to applicants from all countries including Cambodia; apply online through the Türkiye Bursları application system; interviews may be arranged through the Turkish Embassy in Phnom Penh.
deadline_note: Opens around 10 January and closes around 20 February each year (2026 cycle: 10 January – 20 February 2026); the 2027 cycle is expected in January–February 2027
language_req: No test required at application; programmes are taught in Turkish (one-year preparatory course provided) or English

name: France Excellence Eiffel Scholarship Programme
provider: French Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs – managed by Campus France
fields: Science and technology (biology and health, ecological transition, mathematics and digital, engineering sciences) and humanities and social sciences (French and European history and civilisation, law and political science, economics and management)
covers: monthly allowance of EUR 1,200 (master) or EUR 2,100 (PhD)
eligibility: Non-French nationality; age limits set in each call (recent calls: no older than 27 for master's and 32 for PhD); candidates are nominated by the French higher education institution that admits them – students cannot apply directly; currently enrolled or admitted to a master's or doctoral programme in France
cambodia_note: Cambodians are eligible but must be proposed by a French university or grande école; Campus France Cambodge at the Institut français du Cambodge in Phnom Penh advises candidates on securing a nomination.
deadline_note: Call opens 1 October each year; institutions must submit nominations to Campus France by early January (the 2026 call closed 8 January 2026) with results at the end of March; the 2027 call is expected October 2026 – January 2027
language_req: French or English depending on the programme; no fixed test score in the scholarship rules

name: Bourses France Excellence – Embassy of France in Cambodia (formerly BGF)
provider: Embassy of France in Cambodia (French Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs), co-financed with Cambodian partner institutions
fields: Any field (2026-2027 campaign: co-funded doctorates; earlier campaigns also funded master's degrees)
covers: international travel (co-financed with the partner institution)
eligibility: Cambodian nationality; letter of acceptance or pre-acceptance from a French institution; agreement in principle from a thesis supervisor in a French laboratory; mandatory co-financing agreement with a partner institution such as the Ministry of Education, Youth and Sport (MoEYS) or the Cambodia Academy of Digital Technology (CADT)
cambodia_note: Cambodia-specific programme run by the French Embassy in Phnom Penh with Campus France Cambodge; the 2026-2027 doctoral campaign ran 16 March – 27 April 2026 (22:00). Results are published on the embassy website.
deadline_note: Opens in mid-March and closes in late April each year; the next campaign is expected March–April 2027
language_req: French or English depending on the host laboratory

name: ARES Scholarships for International Training (Bourses de formations internationales)
provider: ARES – Académie de recherche et d'enseignement supérieur (Fédération Wallonie-Bruxelles, Belgian development cooperation)
fields: Development-related specialised master's degrees and short advanced training courses at French-speaking Belgian universities (public health, environment, water, agronomy, economics, IT, transport, etc.)
eligibility: National of and resident in one of ARES's partner countries (Cambodia included); relevant degree; at least 2 years of relevant professional experience for specialised masters; age limits (under 40 for masters, under 45 for short courses at the start of training); proficiency in French (most programmes) or English
cambodia_note: Cambodia is one of the roughly 29–31 ARES partner countries; Cambodian candidates apply directly online through the ARES application form for the 2027-2028 call – no embassy step.
deadline_note: Call published in August with a deadline in September each year (the 2027-2028 call document was published August 2026; aggregators list 18 September 2026 as the deadline – verify on the ARES page)

name: VLIR-UOS ICP Connect Scholarships
provider: VLIR-UOS – Flemish Interuniversity Council, University Development Cooperation (funded by the Belgian government)
fields: Development-relevant English-taught master programmes at Flemish universities (water resources, epidemiology, food technology, sustainable development, governance, etc.)
eligibility: National of and resident in one of the VLIR-UOS scholarship countries (Cambodia included); no older than 35 (initial master) or 45 (advanced master) on 1 January of the intake year; preference for candidates employed in higher education, government or civil society; must meet the programme's admission requirements
cambodia_note: Cambodia is one of the 29 VLIR-UOS scholarship countries; Cambodian applicants apply to the ICP Connect master programme directly and request the scholarship in the same application.
deadline_note: The 2027-2028 call is expected to open in mid-November 2026; programme deadlines usually fall between February and March 2027
language_req: English (typically IELTS 6.5 / TOEFL iBT 80–90 as set by the programme)

name: Government of Ireland International Education Scholarships (GOI-IES)
provider: Government of Ireland – Higher Education Authority (HEA)
fields: Any field at NFQ level 9 (taught/research master's, postgraduate diploma) or level 10 (PhD) at eligible Irish higher education institutions
covers: EUR 10,000 stipend for one year of full-time study
full waiver of tuition fees and registration charge for the scholarship year
eligibility: Domiciled outside the EU/EEA, Switzerland and the UK; conditional or final offer of admission to an eligible Irish institution at the time of application; two references uploaded via the online portal; 60 awards per year
cambodia_note: Cambodians apply directly to the HEA online portal once they hold an offer from an Irish institution; no embassy involvement.
deadline_note: Opens in late January and closes in March each year (2026 call closed 12 March 2026 at 17:00 Irish time); the 2027 call is expected January–March 2027
language_req: Must meet the host institution's English requirement (typically IELTS 6.5)

name: Italian Government Scholarships for Foreign Students (MAECI)
provider: Italian Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation (MAECI)
fields: Any field: master's degrees (laurea magistrale), AFAM arts/music/dance programmes, PhD, research projects under academic supervision, and Italian language and culture courses
covers: monthly grant of EUR 900 (EUR 10,800 for a 12-month scholarship; EUR 3,600 for language courses)
tuition fee exemption at the host institution (per institution rules)
eligibility: Citizen of an eligible country (Cambodia is on the 2026-2027 list); age under 28 for master's/AFAM/language courses, under 30 for PhD and under 40 for research; academic qualification for the chosen course; Italian language B2 or, for English-taught courses, English B2
cambodia_note: Cambodia appears on MAECI's list of eligible countries; Cambodians apply online through the Study in Italy portal (studyinitaly.esteri.it), with the Embassy of Italy in Phnom Penh as reference point.
deadline_note: Call published around February/March with a deadline in late March or April each year (2026-2027 call closed 26 March 2026 at 14:00 CET); the 2027-2028 call is expected February–March 2027
language_req: Italian B2, or English B2 for English-taught programmes

name: Czech Government Scholarships for Developing Countries
provider: Government of the Czech Republic – Ministry of Education, Youth and Sports (Foreign Development Cooperation)
fields: Selected follow-up master's and doctoral programmes in technical fields, agriculture, economics and natural sciences at Czech public universities
covers: monthly stipend of CZK 16,000 (master) or CZK 24,960 (PhD)
accommodation and meals at subsidised student rates
health care under Czech public insurance
Czech language preparatory course for Czech-taught programmes
eligibility: Cambodian citizen not permanently resident in the Czech Republic; bachelor degree for master's programmes or master's degree for doctoral programmes; good English (or Czech after preparatory year); travel costs are not covered
cambodia_note: Cambodia is one of the 13 eligible countries. Apply through the MEYS online portal; the Embassy of the Czech Republic in Phnom Penh announces the call each year and coordinates with Cambodian applicants. The 2027/2028 round runs 21 August – 30 September 2026.
deadline_note: Opens in late July/August and closes 30 September each year (2027/2028: 21 August – 30 September 2026)
language_req: English (programmes in English) or Czech after a preparatory language year

name: National Scholarship Programme of the Slovak Republic (NSP)
provider: Government of the Slovak Republic – Ministry of Education, administered by SAIA
fields: Any field – study stays for master's students (1–2 semesters), research stays for PhD students, and teaching/research stays for university teachers, researchers and artists (1–10 months)
covers: monthly scholarship of EUR 620 (master's students) or EUR 1,025.50 and up (PhD students, researchers, teachers, depending on experience)
travel allowance for international students and PhD students based on distance
eligibility: Open to applicants from any country; master's students must be enrolled abroad and come for a 1–2 semester stay (not a full degree); PhD students and researchers need an acceptance/invitation letter from a Slovak host university or research institute; no age limit
cambodia_note: No country restrictions, so Cambodian nationals apply directly online at scholarships.sk; no embassy nomination.
deadline_note: Two rounds each year: 31 October (16:00 CET) for stays in the summer semester, and 30 April for stays in the winter semester of the next academic year
language_req: Language of the host institution (English or Slovak); no fixed test score

name: Romanian Government Scholarships for Foreign Citizens (MFA)
provider: Government of Romania – Ministry of Foreign Affairs
fields: Any field except medicine, dentistry and pharmacy
covers: monthly stipend (approximately EUR 65 bachelor, EUR 75 master, EUR 85 PhD equivalent in RON)
eligibility: Citizen of a non-EU country (Cambodia eligible); average grade of at least 7/10 (or 'good') in previous studies; age under 35 for bachelor's and under 45 for master's/PhD; bachelor's and master's programmes are taught in Romanian (after a preparatory year); PhD may be in English or another foreign language; international travel and other costs not covered
cambodia_note: Cambodians apply directly online through the StudyInRomania platform ('Apply for MFA scholarships'); the Embassy of Romania accredited to Cambodia (in Bangkok) can be consulted.
deadline_note: Opens mid-February and closes 31 March each year (2026-2027 window: 16 February – 31 March 2026, results around 15 July); the 2027-2028 call is expected February–March 2027
language_req: Romanian (preparatory year provided) for bachelor's/master's; English possible at PhD level

name: Open Doors: Russian Scholarship Project (International Olympiad)
provider: Government of the Russian Federation – Ministry of Science and Higher Education, run by the Association of Global Universities
fields: 14+ subject areas including engineering, computer science, physics, chemistry, biology, mathematics, economics, medicine, education, linguistics, political science and more
covers: tuition-free study under the Russian Government education quota
monthly state stipend as a quota student
eligibility: Foreign citizens or stateless persons with the previous level of education completed (or completing it in the year of the olympiad): secondary education (bachelor track), bachelor (master track), master/specialist (doctoral track), PhD (postdoctoral track); no age limit; selection via online portfolio, testing and, for the doctoral track, interview; international travel and insurance not covered
cambodia_note: Open to all foreign citizens including Cambodians; register directly on the Open Doors website – winners receive a quota place without going through the embassy competition. Registration for the 2026/27 olympiad runs 20 August – 1 November 2026.
deadline_note: Registration opens 20 August and closes around 1 November each year (portfolio stage until mid-November), with further stages in November–February
language_req: English or Russian (working languages of the olympiad; programme language depends on university)

name: Russian Government Quota Scholarship (Rossotrudnichestvo)
provider: Government of the Russian Federation – Ministry of Science and Higher Education / Rossotrudnichestvo
fields: Wide range including engineering, IT, nuclear and civil engineering, medicine, economics, law, international relations, arts, culture and tourism
covers: tuition-free study at a Russian state university
preparatory Russian language year where needed
eligibility: Cambodian citizen with the required prior qualification (secondary certificate, bachelor or master); selection through the national competition organised with Cambodia's Ministry of Education, Youth and Sport and the Russian House in Phnom Penh; international travel and medical insurance are at the student's expense
cambodia_note: Cambodia receives an annual quota (MoEYS announced 40 places for 2025-2026 for students and civil servants). Candidates register on education-in-russia.com and are selected via MoEYS and the Russian Centre for Science and Culture (Russian House), Preah Norodom Blvd, Phnom Penh (tel. 023 213 508).
deadline_note: Registration on education-in-russia.com usually opens in the autumn with country selection deadlines between December and March; check MoEYS and Russian House Phnom Penh announcements for the 2027/28 dates
language_req: Russian (preparatory year available) or English for selected programmes

name: Canada-ASEAN Scholarships and Educational Exchanges for Development (SEED-2)
provider: Global Affairs Canada
fields: Study or research linked to the UN Sustainable Development Goals (poverty reduction, climate action, gender equality, etc.), 4–8 month exchanges
covers: tuition-waived exchange at the Canadian host institution (value roughly CAD 10,200–15,900 depending on level and duration)
eligibility: Citizen of an ASEAN member state including Cambodia; enrolled full-time at a home institution that has an exchange agreement with a Canadian college or university; short-term study/research of 4–8 months; not holding Canadian citizenship/permanent residence or a pending application
cambodia_note: Cambodian students cannot apply directly: the Canadian partner institution submits the application on their behalf, so candidates must go through their home university's international office and its Canadian partner.
deadline_note: Canadian institutions submit applications around March each year for exchanges starting from August; the 2027-2028 call is expected in early 2027
language_req: English or French as required by the Canadian host institution

name: MASHAV Professional Training Courses in Israel
provider: MASHAV – Israel's Agency for International Development Cooperation, Ministry of Foreign Affairs
fields: Short professional courses (2–4 weeks) in agriculture, water management, education, public health, entrepreneurship and innovation, community development, gender equality and more
eligibility: Professionals from developing countries with a relevant academic degree or professional background and current employment in the course field; good command of English; typically aged 25–50; international airfare is paid by the participant or a sponsor
cambodia_note: Cambodians apply for individual courses through the MASHAV online form and are screened by the Embassy of Israel in Phnom Penh; Cambodia and Israel signed an education cooperation MoU in February 2026.
deadline_note: Course-by-course deadlines year-round, usually 6–8 weeks before each course starts (e.g., 1 June 2026 for some mid-2026 courses)

name: NL Scholarship (formerly Holland Scholarship)
provider: Dutch Ministry of Education, Culture and Science together with participating Dutch universities
fields: Any field offered by the participating Dutch research universities and universities of applied sciences
covers: one-off EUR 5,000 paid in the first year of study
eligibility: Nationality outside the European Economic Area (Cambodia qualifies); applying for a full-time bachelor's or master's programme at a participating Dutch institution; must meet the institution's admission requirements; not previously enrolled in a Dutch degree programme
cambodia_note: Cambodians apply through the participating institution's own NL Scholarship procedure after applying for admission; no embassy step.
deadline_note: Institution deadlines usually fall between 1 February and 1 May for the September intake

name: MoEYS National Scholarship for Bachelor's Degree (state-funded places for Bac II graduates)
provider: Ministry of Education, Youth and Sport (MoEYS), Department of Scholarships / Royal Government of Cambodia
fields: any field offered at public universities and institutes (RUPP, ITC, NUM, RULE, RUA, UHS, IFL, NPIC, regional universities etc.); each institution has a quota
covers: tuition (state-funded place, fees waived for the whole bachelor's)
eligibility: Cambodian nationals who passed the grade-12 national exam (Bac II) in the current year; ranked by exam grade; priority for students from poor families (IDPoor), female students, students from remote/rural provinces, ethnic minorities, orphans and students with disabilities; no living stipend
cambodia_note: Domestic program run entirely by MoEYS. Apply online through the MoEYS scholarship application system using your Bac II candidate number during the window announced right after exam results; choose an institution and major; results published on moeys.gov.kh and the MoEYS Facebook page. Confirm the current-cycle notice on the official site.
deadline_note: Announced immediately after Bac II results; usually opens in September and closes roughly two to three weeks later (September–October); first-year classes start November–December
verdict: Not verifiable online in this session: moeys.gov.kh (and every secondary source tried) is blocked by the network egress proxy and the web-search budget was exhausted; kept because this is MoEYS's long-running annual state scholarship for Bac II graduates, with the 2026 window still to be confirmed on the official site.

provider: Royal Government of Cambodia (Office of the Prime Minister) administered through MoEYS
fields: any; recipient chooses a university in Cambodia (public or participating private university)
covers: tuition for the full bachelor's degree at the chosen Cambodian university
eligibility: Cambodian students who obtain Grade A in the current year's Bac II (grade-12) national exam; awarded to all Grade-A students
cambodia_note: Automatically offered to every Grade-A Bac II student via MoEYS after results are released; students register their choice of university through the MoEYS scholarship system. Domestic only. Verify the current-year announcement on moeys.gov.kh.
deadline_note: Follows the Bac II results each year (results early–mid September; registration September–October)

name: MoEYS Teacher Trainee Recruitment (Teacher Education Colleges, Regional Teacher Training Centres, NIE)
provider: Ministry of Education, Youth and Sport (MoEYS), Teacher Training Department
fields: teacher education: primary (12+2), lower-secondary (12+2 / 12+4 Bachelor of Education at Phnom Penh and Battambang Teacher Education Colleges), upper-secondary (bachelor graduates, 1 year at National Institute of Education)
covers: appointment as a civil-servant teacher on completion
eligibility: Cambodian nationals; Bac II pass for 12+2 and 12+4 tracks, bachelor's degree for the NIE 12+4+1 track; age limit set in each year's announcement (generally under about 30); must pass the annual teacher-recruitment entrance exam; provincial quotas
cambodia_note: Domestic program; recruitment notice published on moeys.gov.kh and at provincial education offices after Bac II results; apply at the provincial office of education or online, then sit the entrance exam
deadline_note: Recruitment announced each year after Bac II results, usually September–October with the entrance exam in October–November
verdict: Not verifiable online in this session: moeys.gov.kh and secondary sources are blocked by the egress proxy and the search budget is exhausted; kept because teacher-trainee recruitment is an annual MoEYS process, but the 2026 notice, quotas, age limits and dates are unconfirmed.
changes: none (confidence lowered because the page could not be fetched)
