language_km: ខ្មែរ រៀនអង់គ្លេសបន្ថែមក្នុងវគ្គ

name: SHE-CAN Scholar Program (Cambodia)
provider: SHE-CAN (US non-profit)
fields: any (undergraduate degree at a US college or university)
covers: mentoring and leadership training in the US
support to win a full-ride scholarship (tuition, housing) at a top US college
eligibility: Cambodian women aged 17-20 graduating secondary school by June 2027, from low-income/low-opportunity backgrounds, living within about 1 hour of Phnom Penh, strong English, academic excellence and demonstrated leadership, less than 1 year of post-secondary credits, able to dedicate Dec 2026-Jun 2027 to the online pre-college program
cambodia_note: Cambodia is one of three SHE-CAN countries; apply through the Cambodia Scholar Application 2026-27 form (Trakstar) with Grade 10-12 transcripts and national exam score report in PDF; accepted scholars apply to US colleges for the 2028-29 academic year
deadline_note: Applications usually open in July and close 1 October each year; 2026-27 cycle closes 1 October 2026
language_req: strong spoken and written English (must later pass TOEFL/Duolingo for US colleges)

name: Teach For Cambodia Fellowship
provider: Teach For Cambodia (NGO, Teach For All network)
fields: any degree background; two-year teaching and leadership fellowship in Cambodian public schools
covers: educational award package and alumni network
eligibility: Cambodian nationals with at least a bachelor's degree in any major (recent graduates, young professionals or existing public/private teachers); no teaching experience required; must commit full-time for two years, cohorts start in October
cambodia_note: Program is only for Cambodians; apply online via the TFC application form (tfaforms), then interview and assessment; questions to recruitment@teachforcambodia.org
deadline_note: Applications for each cohort open in stages through the year with several deadlines; cohort begins in October

name: Cambodia Rural Students Trust (CRST) Scholarship
provider: Cambodia Rural Students Trust (local NGO, Siem Reap)
fields: any (private high school then university in Siem Reap)
eligibility: Bright students from poor rural families in Siem Reap area with passion for education and desire to help others; selected on merit and financial need; up to 20 new students a year
cambodia_note: Cambodia-only; candidates go through three stages: written test, interview and home visit; contact CRST in Siem Reap via the website contact page
deadline_note: Annual intake with testing before the school year; exact dates announced locally

name: Ponheary Ly Foundation University & Vocational Training Scholarships
provider: Ponheary Ly Foundation (US/Cambodian NGO, Siem Reap)
fields: any; about 65% of awards go to STEM (medicine, engineering, IT) plus vocational trades (mechanics, culinary)
eligibility: High school graduates, primarily from PLF-supported rural schools in Siem Reap province, with strong academic skills (university) or aptitude for vocational training; priority to young women
cambodia_note: Cambodia-only; students apply after Grade 12 graduation through PLF staff in Siem Reap; enquiries by email via theplf.org
deadline_note: Applications taken after the national Grade 12 exam for the academic year starting late in the year

name: AUPP Liger Leadership Academy Residential Scholarship
provider: Liger Charitable Foundation / AUPP Liger Leadership Academy
fields: STEEAM (science, technology, entrepreneurship, engineering, arts, math) secondary education
covers: medical and dental care, health insurance
tuition (full scholarship historically covered tuition, room and board, clothing, medical and dental care, insurance, school supplies and transport)
scholarship places now mixed with fee-paying places (2025/26 tuition USD 13,500 plus USD 1,600 capital fee)
eligibility: Cambodian children entering Grade 7-8 who are educationally, economically and/or geographically disadvantaged; selection by school records, student interview with Education Director and family interview; no test; school now also admits fee-paying students
cambodia_note: Cambodia-only; submit the enrollment form online or downloaded (Khmer form available), with birth certificate; no application fee
deadline_note: Rolling admissions; apply before the first semester (August) or second semester (January); decision within a week of interview
name_km: អាហារូបករណ៍ AUPP Liger Leadership Academy
provider_km: Liger Leadership Academy / សាកលវិទ្យាល័យអាមេរិកាំងភ្នំពេញ (AUPP)
summary_km: សាលាអន្តេវាសិកនៅភ្នំពេញ សម្រាប់សិស្សចូលរៀនថ្នាក់ទី 7 ឬទី 8 ដែលរៀនផ្តោតលើ STEM សហគ្រិនភាព និងភាពជាអ្នកដឹកនាំ។ មានអាហារូបករណ៍មួយចំនួនសម្រាប់សិស្សដែលមានឱកាសតិច ប៉ុន្តែឥឡូវនេះសាលាមានកន្លែងបង់ថ្លៃផងដែរ។
summary_en: Residential grade 7-12 school in Phnom Penh with a STEM, entrepreneurship and leadership curriculum; a limited number of scholarship places for disadvantaged students alongside fee-paying places.
eligibility_km: សិស្សខ្មែរចូលរៀនថ្នាក់ទី 7 ឬទី 8 ជ្រើសរើសតាមសំណៅពិន្ទុ និងការសម្ភាសជាមួយសិស្ស និងគ្រួសារ
covers_km: ថ្លៃសិក្សា កន្លែងស្នាក់នៅ និងអាហារ (អាស្រ័យលើអាហារូបករណ៍ដែលទទួលបាន)
deadline_km: ទទួលពាក្យពេញមួយឆ្នាំ មុនឆមាសខែសីហា ឬខែមករា
fields_km: ថ្នាក់ទី 7 ដល់ទី 12 (STEM សហគ្រិនភាព ភាពជាអ្នកដឹកនាំ)
cambodia_km: ទាក់ទងការិយាល័យចុះឈ្មោះរបស់សាលានៅភ្នំពេញដោយផ្ទាល់ ហើយសួរអំពីអាហារូបករណ៍ដែលមាន។
language_km: រៀនជាភាសាអង់គ្លេស មិនទាមទារវិញ្ញាបនបត្រ

name: Jay Pritzker Academy Full Academic Scholarship
provider: Jay Pritzker Academy (private foundation school, Siem Reap)
fields: K-12 international college-preparatory curriculum with AP courses
covers: full tuition from kindergarten to Grade 12
eligibility: Children aged four from rural villages of Puok District, Siem Reap Province; about 60 places a year, all admitted students receive full scholarships
cambodia_note: Cambodia-only and limited to Puok District families; recruitment done locally by the school each year
deadline_note: Annual intake of four-year-olds before the school year; dates announced locally

name: Cambodian Scholarship Foundation (CASF) Girls' Scholarship
provider: Cambodian Scholarship Foundation (US non-profit)
fields: any
covers: secondary school support and local educational coordinator
medical care, computer lab and mentoring
eligibility: Adolescent girls from Kandal and Svay Rieng provinces showing motivation, merit and financial need; university support continues once the student passes the national exam and is accepted to university
cambodia_note: Cambodia-only, limited to Kandal and Svay Rieng; students identified through local communities and CASF coordinators rather than an open online form
deadline_note: Selection around the start of lower secondary school; no published window

name: Cambodian Village Fund Scholarship Program
provider: Cambodian Village Fund (US non-profit)
fields: any (universities in Battambang such as National University of Battambang)
covers: room and board in CVF scholarship house in Battambang
eligibility: Students in grades 7-12 and high school graduates from very poor families in CVF's partner villages (Battambang area) at risk of dropping out for financial reasons and committed to continuing to college
cambodia_note: Cambodia-only; candidates identified by a village screening committee (CVF English teachers, school officials, operations manager), then student and parents submit an application; final selection by CVF board
deadline_note: Selected annually before the school year; no public deadline

name: Lotus Outreach GATE and CATALYST Scholarships for Girls
provider: Lotus Outreach International / Lotus Outreach Cambodia
fields: any
covers: GATE (grades 7-12): school materials, uniforms, transportation, rice support for family, protective housing for some
CATALYST (tertiary): tuition, food, residence, utilities, class fees, daily allowance
leadership and professional development seminars, mentoring
eligibility: At-risk girls from families in extreme poverty in Phnom Penh, Siem Reap and Banteay Meanchey (GATE); CATALYST university scholarships go to GATE graduates who pass Grade 12
cambodia_note: Cambodia-only; girls are identified through Lotus Outreach Cambodia's community partners and schools; CATALYST applications come from GATE graduates
deadline_note: Annual selection tied to the school year; no public deadline

name: JWOC (Journeys Within Our Community) University Scholarship Program
provider: Journeys Within Our Community (local NGO, Siem Reap)
fields: any (universities in Siem Reap)
covers: English, computer, life-skills, career guidance and leadership training
eligibility: Cambodian high school graduates from Siem Reap or other provinces with demonstrated desire for higher education, willingness to help their community, past academic performance and financial need; scholars give back through volunteering
cambodia_note: Cambodia-only; JWOC announces the call through high schools, NGOs and social media; application forms collected at the JWOC office in Siem Reap or downloaded online
deadline_note: Annual call usually after the Grade 12 exam results, before the university year starts

name: Child's Dream University Scholarship Programme - Cambodia (Bachelor level)
provider: Child's Dream Foundation (Swiss charity, Chiang Mai)
fields: any, at Cambodian universities
eligibility: Academically strong, financially disadvantaged Cambodian high school graduates who could not otherwise afford tertiary education; typically four-year support
cambodia_note: Cambodia-specific programme; application via the Child's Dream 'Apply for Scholarships' page and its Cambodia partner office; enquiries to info@childsdream.org
deadline_note: Annual call published on the Child's Dream website, usually before the Cambodian university year

name: Child's Dream University Scholarships (International Bachelor's, Thailand)
provider: Child's Dream Foundation
fields: any, at partner universities in Thailand
eligibility: Academically strong, disadvantaged high school graduates from Cambodia, Myanmar, Laos and Thailand with good English, meeting the admission requirements of the partner Thai universities
cambodia_note: Cambodia is one of the four eligible countries; apply online via childsdream.org; contact uspib@childsdream.org
deadline_note: Application period December to January; the 2025 intake closed 28 February 2025; similar window expected for the 2027 intake

name: Cambodian Children's Fund University Scholarships
provider: Cambodian Children's Fund (NGO, Phnom Penh)
fields: any
eligibility: Students enrolled in CCF's education programs (Steung Meanchey area, Phnom Penh) who graduate Grade 12 and are accepted to university or vocational training; about 70% of CCF students go on to university
cambodia_note: Cambodia-only and limited to CCF students; CCF also nominates top female students to the SHE-CAN US scholarship and Trinity College Melbourne scholarships
deadline_note: Internal selection after the Grade 12 national exam each year

name: Empowering Youth in Cambodia (EYC) High School and University Scholarship Support
provider: Empowering Youth in Cambodia (local NGO, Phnom Penh)
fields: any
covers: English, digital literacy and STEM courses
eligibility: Young people from low-income families attending EYC's three community centres in Phnom Penh who show strong academic potential
cambodia_note: Cambodia-only; students apply through their EYC community centre
deadline_note: Selected each academic year; no public deadline

name: This Life Cambodia Scholarship and Student Assistance Program
provider: This Life Cambodia (local NGO, Siem Reap)
fields: any
eligibility: Poorest students in Siem Reap, Banteay Meanchey and Kandal provinces, with a specific scholarship stream for children whose parents are in conflict with the law
cambodia_note: Cambodia-only; selection through This Life Cambodia community and school programs
deadline_note: Annual selection tied to the school year

name: Room to Read Cambodia Girls' Education Program
provider: Room to Read (international NGO)
fields: lower and upper secondary school (grades 7-12)
covers: boarding scholarships (housing, food, books) for girls living far from school
eligibility: Cambodian girls aged 12-18 in grades 7-12 enrolled at partner public secondary schools in five provinces (about 40 schools); selected on need
cambodia_note: No open application; girls are enrolled through participating schools and community mentors (social mobilisers), so ask the school director whether the school is a Room to Read partner
deadline_note: Enrolment through partner schools at the start of each school year (around November)
name_km: កម្មវិធីអប់រំកុមារី Room to Read កម្ពុជា
provider_km: អង្គការ Room to Read (អង្គការមិនមែនរដ្ឋាភិបាលអន្តរជាតិ)
summary_km: កម្មវិធីជួយឱ្យកុមារីកម្ពុជាបានបន្តរៀនពីថ្នាក់ទី 7 ដល់ទី 12 រហូតចប់វិទ្យាល័យ។ ទទួលបានសម្ភារសិក្សា ឯកសណ្ឋាន ការធ្វើដំណើរ កន្លែងស្នាក់នៅសម្រាប់អ្នកនៅឆ្ងាយ និងការណែនាំពីអ្នកណែនាំ។
summary_en: Helps Cambodian girls stay in school from grade 7 through grade 12. Provides school materials, uniforms, transport, boarding for girls who live far away, and mentoring with life-skills sessions.
eligibility_km: កុមារីអាយុ 12-18 ឆ្នាំ រៀនថ្នាក់ទី 7 ដល់ទី 12 នៅសាលារដ្ឋដៃគូក្នុង 5 ខេត្ត ជ្រើសរើសតាមតម្រូវការគ្រួសារ
covers_km: សម្ភារសិក្សា ឯកសណ្ឋាន ថ្លៃធ្វើដំណើរ កន្លែងស្នាក់នៅ និងអាហារសម្រាប់អ្នកនៅឆ្ងាយ ព្រមទាំងការណែនាំជំនាញជីវិត
deadline_km: ជ្រើសរើសនៅដើមឆ្នាំសិក្សានីមួយៗ ប្រហែលខែវិច្ឆិកា
fields_km: ការសិក្សាទូទៅកម្រិតមធ្យមសិក្សា ថ្នាក់ទី 7-12
cambodia_km: មិនមានការដាក់ពាក្យតាមអនឡាញទេ។ សួរនាយកសាលា ឬគ្រូណែនាំថាតើសាលារបស់អ្នកជាដៃគូ Room to Read ឬអត់ ព្រោះការជ្រើសរើសធ្វើឡើងតាមរយៈសាលា។
language_km: មិនទាមទារ
also_known_as: Room to Read Girls' Education Program Cambodia

name: YSEALI Professional Fellows Program
provider: U.S. Department of State (Young Southeast Asian Leaders Initiative)
fields: Civic engagement, NGO management, economic empowerment, governance and legislative process, environmental and natural resources management
eligibility: Emerging leaders aged 25-35 from ASEAN countries (including Cambodia) working in one of the program themes, with professional experience and English proficiency sufficient for a four-week U.S. work placement; five weeks total in the United States.
cambodia_note: Cambodia is one of the ten ASEAN countries covered by YSEALI. Applications are submitted online through the program website (www.ysealipfp.org); Cambodia-specific questions go to the U.S. Embassy YSEALI team (YSEALICambodia@state.gov). Check current status, as the related YSEALI Academic Fellows program is paused.
deadline_note: Cycles have historically been announced once or twice a year on the program website; no 2026-2027 deadline confirmed.

name: Study of the U.S. Institutes (SUSI) for Secondary Educators
provider: U.S. Department of State; recruited by the U.S. Embassy Phnom Penh Public Diplomacy Section
fields: U.S. society, culture, values and institutions for secondary school teachers, administrators, teacher trainers, curriculum developers and ministry of education officials
covers: round-trip transportation to the United States
eligibility: Mid-career secondary educators, typically aged 30-50, experienced and highly motivated, with English fluency; five-week intensive post-graduate-level institute (Summer 2026 institutes hosted by the University of Montana). U.S. citizens and green-card holders not eligible.
cambodia_note: Cambodian educators email the completed SUSI application form to PDExchanges@state.gov (subject 'SUSIs for Secondary Educators – Summer 2026'); the form is downloaded from the U.S. Embassy Cambodia page. The embassy also periodically recruits Cambodian undergraduates for SUSI Student Leaders institutes.
deadline_note: Embassy call for the summer institutes is usually published in the preceding autumn/winter; Summer 2026 call posted on the embassy site. Check the page for the next summer's deadline.

name: Fulbright Teaching Excellence and Achievement (TEA) Program
provider: U.S. Department of State, implemented by IREX; recruited by the U.S. Embassy Phnom Penh
fields: Secondary-school teaching (English, social studies, mathematics, science, special education)
eligibility: Secondary-level teachers with several years of full-time classroom experience, a bachelor's degree or equivalent, and English proficiency; six-week professional development program at a U.S. university with a school practicum.
cambodia_note: The U.S. Embassy in Cambodia posts the annual TEA call for Cambodian teachers on its website (2026-2027 program page); applications are submitted online through IREX with embassy nomination.
deadline_note: Embassy call for each program year usually published in early-to-mid year; consult the 2026-2027 TEA page for the exact date.

name: JENESYS Phase III (Japan-ASEAN Network of Exchange for Sustainable Partnership)
provider: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Japan, implemented by Japan International Cooperation Center (JICE)
fields: Social business and economic/social exchange themes between Japan and ASEAN
eligibility: University students, graduate students or young professionals from Japan and ASEAN member states, up to 30 years old during the program period; ability to take part in lectures, site visits and group presentations in English. Roughly two weeks in Japan and Thailand.
cambodia_note: Cambodia is an ASEAN member and JENESYS batches are regularly organised for Cambodian youth. Recruitment is through JICE's public call and, for other JENESYS batches, via nomination by the Embassy of Japan in Cambodia and Cambodian ministries/universities.
deadline_note: JICE call published in October 2025 for the Phase III program; other JENESYS batches are announced throughout the Japanese fiscal year with a few weeks to apply.

name: Ship for Southeast Asian and Japanese Youth Program (SSEAYP)
provider: Cabinet Office, Government of Japan, with ASEAN member governments (Cambodia: Ministry of Education, Youth and Sport)
fields: any (youth leadership, cultural exchange, discussion programs)
covers: accommodation aboard the ship and in Japan
eligibility: Participating youths aged 18-30 (Cambodia's General Department of Youth has recruited Khmer nationals aged 18-33), with good English, leadership record and ability to join the full multi-week voyage. Cambodia joined SSEAYP in 2000.
cambodia_note: Cambodian delegates (around 10 per year) are selected by the General Department of Youth of the Ministry of Education, Youth and Sport, which publishes the recruitment notice. Cambodia will host a port of call for the 50th SSEAYP in 2027 (Preah Sihanouk and Phnom Penh).
deadline_note: MoEYS recruitment usually runs a few months before the voyage; 50th program scheduled for early 2027 with the Cambodia port call in January 2027.

name: ASEAN Youth Fellowship (AYF)
provider: Singapore International Foundation and National Youth Council Singapore (Singapore-ASEAN Youth Fund)
fields: any (regional leadership development for young professionals)
eligibility: Young professional leaders aged 27-35 who are nationals of an ASEAN member state (including Cambodia), with a record of leadership and impact and working proficiency in English; one-week residential program (2026 edition 13-20 November 2026 in Singapore and Manila).
cambodia_note: Cambodian nationals apply directly online via the SIF/NYC application form; Cambodia has fellows in every cohort. AYF 2026 applications closed 31 May 2026.
deadline_note: Opens around March-April and closes end of May each year for a November program.

name: Obama Foundation Leaders Asia-Pacific
provider: The Obama Foundation
fields: any (values-based leadership for changemakers in government, civil society and private sector)
covers: travel and accommodation for in-person convenings
eligibility: Aged 24-45 on 1 September of the program year, at least three years of relevant experience in their issue area, professionally proficient in English, and currently residing in an eligible Asia-Pacific country or territory; eight-month non-residential program combining virtual sessions and in-person gatherings.
cambodia_note: Cambodia is explicitly listed among eligible Asia-Pacific countries; Cambodians apply online directly to the Obama Foundation.
deadline_note: Applications for the 2026-2027 cohort opened November 2025 and are now closed; the 2027-2028 call is expected to open around November 2026.

name: Rotary Peace Fellowship
provider: The Rotary Foundation (Rotary International)
fields: Peace, conflict resolution and development studies (master's degree or professional development certificate)
eligibility: Open to all nationalities. Bachelor's degree, strong academic record, English proficiency; master's track needs about three years of related work experience, certificate track at least five years; at least three years must have passed since the last academic degree; applicants must be endorsed by a Rotary district. Rotarians and their close relatives are ineligible.
cambodia_note: Cambodians apply online through My Rotary and must obtain endorsement from a Rotary district (Cambodia's clubs are in District 3350). The 2027-28 application has closed.
deadline_note: Opens in February and closes 15 May each year; the 2028-29 application opens February 2027 with deadline 15 May 2027.

name: KOICA Fellowship Program (CIAT) - Capacity Improvement and Advancement for Tomorrow
provider: Korea International Cooperation Agency (KOICA), Government of Korea
fields: Public administration, economic development, climate change, health, agriculture, education, digital/ICT and other development sectors
eligibility: Public-sector officials and professionals from KOICA partner countries nominated by their government, generally with relevant field experience and working English; short-term country-focused and multi-country training courses in Korea (weeks). KOICA also runs 17-month master's scholarships under the same scheme.
cambodia_note: Cambodia is a KOICA partner country; candidates are nominated by Cambodian ministries and submitted through the KOICA Cambodia Office in Phnom Penh (koica.go.kr/sites/khm_en). Individual applications must go via the relevant ministry.
deadline_note: Courses are announced throughout the year by the KOICA Cambodia Office to line ministries; the master's scholarship track usually closes around July.

name: JICA Knowledge Co-Creation Program (KCCP)
provider: Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA), Government of Japan ODA
fields: Development sectors: tourism, policing, public administration, health, agriculture, infrastructure, environment, education, disaster management and others
eligibility: Officials and professionals from Cambodian government agencies or institutions in the target field of each course, usually with a few years of relevant experience, an age limit set per course, and sufficient English; courses last two weeks to a few months in Japan.
cambodia_note: Cambodia is named as a target country in 2026 courses (e.g., Tourism Marketing and Promotion, Community Policing). Cambodian participants are nominated by their ministry and submitted through the JICA Cambodia Office; individuals cannot apply directly.
deadline_note: Course-by-course deadlines set in each General Information sheet; calls circulate to Cambodian ministries throughout the Japanese fiscal year.

name: Temasek Foundation - NUS Leadership Enrichment and Regional Networking (TF-NUS LEaRN) Programme
provider: Temasek Foundation with National University of Singapore
fields: any (leadership, community engagement and ASEAN networking for undergraduates)
covers: S$1,500 award toward return airfare and living expenses
eligibility: Full-time undergraduates at partner universities in Southeast Asia/ASEAN, nominated by their home university; good English and interest in leadership and community work; roughly two-week residential programme at NUS in July.
cambodia_note: Application is by university nomination only: Cambodian students should ask their university's international office whether it is a TF-NUS LEaRN partner. Similar TF LEaRN programmes run with NTU and SMU.
deadline_note: Partner-university nomination deadline is around mid-March each year for the July programme.

name: Eisenhower Fellowships Global Program
provider: Eisenhower Fellowships (foundation)
fields: any (mid-career leaders from business, government, civil society, academia)
eligibility: Accomplished mid-career leaders (typically in their 30s to mid-40s) with a track record of leadership and impact, citizenship of or at least five years' residence in the country represented, fluent English, and availability for the roughly six-week program (early April to mid-May 2027 for the 2027 cohort).
cambodia_note: Applications are welcomed worldwide, so Cambodians can apply online; candidates from countries with an active Eisenhower Fellowships network are prioritised. 2027 Global Program applications closed in May 2026.
deadline_note: Opens around April and closes mid-May each year for the following spring's program.

name: Hansen Leadership Institute
provider: Hansen Leadership Institute, University of San Diego (Fred J. Hansen Foundation)
fields: any (leadership, conflict resolution, cross-cultural cooperation)
eligibility: University students and recent graduates aged 20-25 at the start of the program, from any country, with strong English and demonstrated leadership; three-week summer institute at the University of San Diego, California.
cambodia_note: Open to all nationalities; Cambodians apply online directly. International applicants have an earlier deadline (15 January 2026 for the 2026 institute).
deadline_note: Applications open in autumn; international deadline is mid-January, U.S. deadline mid-March, for the July program.

name: kanthari Institute for Social Leadership - Social Change Makers Course
provider: kanthari (non-profit institute), Trivandrum, Kerala, India
fields: Social entrepreneurship and founding of social-change organisations
eligibility: Aged 22 or over with no upper age limit, from any country, who have overcome adversity or witnessed a social problem and have a concrete plan to start a social initiative; working English; residential course beginning in April each year.
cambodia_note: Open worldwide, so Cambodian applicants apply directly online; kanthari has hosted participants from Southeast Asia.
deadline_note: Applications usually close in January for the course starting in April of the same year.

name: Asia Foundation Development Fellows
provider: The Asia Foundation
fields: Governance, economic development, women's empowerment, environmental resilience, education and leadership, international cooperation
covers: program costs for U.S. and Asia (Korea) leadership modules
eligibility: Citizens or residents of eligible Asia-Pacific countries including Cambodia, under 40 years old on 1 January of the fellowship year, conversant in English (no TOEFL required), able to obtain a U.S. visa, with a demonstrable record of leadership in the Foundation's fields of expertise.
cambodia_note: Cambodia is an eligible country (The Asia Foundation has a Cambodia office); Cambodians apply online directly.
deadline_note: Call published around late September/October with a deadline in November for the following year's cohort.

name: Korea Foundation Fellowship for Korean Language Training
provider: The Korea Foundation (Government of the Republic of Korea)
fields: Korean language (for Korean studies students, researchers and Korea-related professionals)
eligibility: Undergraduates from Southeast Asia (and other listed regions) majoring or minoring in Korean studies/Korean language, master's or doctoral candidates in Korea-related fields with a research plan, university lecturers and researchers in Korea-related fields, and arts and culture professionals; must already speak at least basic Korean. Six to twelve months at a Korean university language institute.
cambodia_note: Southeast Asia is explicitly listed for undergraduate eligibility, so Cambodian students of Korean language (e.g., at RUPP) can apply online via the KF Application Portal.
deadline_note: Announced annually on the KF Application Portal, usually in the second half of the year for the following year's intake.

name: ASEAN-Korea Youth Network Workshop
provider: ASEAN-Korea Centre (intergovernmental organisation, Seoul)
fields: ASEAN-Korea cooperation, youth networking and thematic workshops
eligibility: Young people (students and young professionals) who are nationals of an ASEAN member state, with good English; about 20 participants selected from the ten ASEAN countries.
cambodia_note: Cambodian nationals apply directly by emailing the application to youth@aseankorea.org during the call period.
deadline_note: 2026 call ran 18 March to 8 April 2026; similar spring window expected in 2027.

name: Millennium Fellowship
provider: United Nations Academic Impact and Millennium Campus Network
fields: any (student-led social impact projects aligned with the SDGs)
covers: free semester-long leadership training on the student's own campus
eligibility: Undergraduate students aged 18 or over enrolled at a college or university anywhere in the world; applicants apply as part of a campus cohort and must commit to a semester of leadership sessions and a social-impact project.
cambodia_note: Open worldwide, so students at Cambodian universities can apply online; the program runs on the student's home campus, not abroad.
deadline_note: Applications for the Class of 2026 closed 28 February 2026; the Class of 2027 application is announced as opening shortly, with a similar early-year deadline expected.

name: Erasmus+ International Credit Mobility (KA171)
provider: European Union (Erasmus+ programme), via European universities and their Cambodian partner universities
fields: any (depends on the inter-institutional agreement between the Cambodian and European university)
eligibility: Students enrolled at a Cambodian university that holds an Erasmus+ KA171 agreement with a European partner; mobility of 2-12 months for study or traineeship, with language level set by the host university (often English B2).
cambodia_note: Cambodia is an eligible partner country; students cannot apply to the EU directly but through their home university's international office (e.g., Institute of Technology of Cambodia with Université de Toulouse, Royal University of Phnom Penh with various EU partners) when the partner university issues a call.
deadline_note: Each European university issues its own calls; many run in spring for the following autumn and in autumn for the spring semester.
language_req: Set by host university, typically English B2

name: AAUW International Fellowships
provider: American Association of University Women (AAUW), US non-profit
fields: Priority for STEM disciplines; any field accepted for master's/doctoral study in the US
covers: Cash fellowship stipend (roughly US$20,000 master's, US$25,000 doctoral, US$50,000 postdoctoral) paid to the fellow
eligibility: Identify as a woman; not a US citizen or permanent resident; hold a degree equivalent to a US bachelor's with minimum cumulative GPA 3.5/4.0; admitted or enrolled in first master's or doctoral program (or postdoctoral research) at an accredited US institution; program must begin on or before 15 Sept 2027 and end after 30 April 2028; commitment to return home / serve women and girls
cambodia_note: Open to women of any non-US nationality; Cambodian women apply directly online, no embassy or MoEYS involvement
deadline_note: Applications open in August and close mid-November each year (15 November in recent cycles); results in April
language_req: English proficiency required (TOEFL/IELTS or waiver if degree taught in English)

name: Margaret McNamara Education Grants (MMEG) - US/Canada Program
provider: Margaret McNamara Education Grants (World Bank family charity)
fields: Any field, with a demonstrated commitment to improving the lives of women and children in developing countries
covers: One-time grant of about US$15,000 towards tuition and living costs
eligibility: Self-identifying woman from an eligible developing country (World Bank low/lower-middle income list); at least 25 years old; already enrolled in an in-person program at an accredited university in the US or Canada (separate programs exist for France, South Africa and Latin America); intends to return to work in a developing country; not related to World Bank Group staff
cambodia_note: Cambodia is a lower-middle-income country and therefore on MMEG's eligibility country list; Cambodian women already enrolled at a US or Canadian university apply online
deadline_note: US-Canada program accepts applications 15 September to 15 January each year; France program 15 October to 15 January

name: P.E.O. International Peace Scholarship (IPS)
provider: P.E.O. Sisterhood (US women's philanthropic organisation)
fields: Any graduate field
covers: Scholarship of up to US$12,500 per academic year towards tuition and living costs
eligibility: Woman who is not a US or Canadian citizen/permanent resident; admitted to full-time graduate study at an accredited institution in the US or Canada; has a full year of coursework remaining; intends to return to her home country after study; must first submit an Eligibility Form
cambodia_note: Cambodian women are eligible; apply online directly to P.E.O. (no embassy or government nomination)
deadline_note: Eligibility forms accepted from about 15 September to 15 December; completed applications due 1 February (already enrolled) or 15 March (not yet enrolled); awards announced in May

name: Zonta International Amelia Earhart Fellowship
provider: Zonta International / Zonta Foundation for Women
fields: Aerospace engineering and space sciences (PhD research)
covers: US$12,000 fellowship, usable at any accredited university worldwide
eligibility: Women of any nationality registered full-time in a PhD/doctoral program in aerospace-applied sciences or engineering; must have completed at least one year of the doctoral program or hold a master's in an aerospace-applied field; must not graduate before April 2028; post-docs and Zonta members not eligible
cambodia_note: Open to women of any nationality; Cambodian women apply directly online
deadline_note: Applications open around August and close 15 November each year; fellows announced in April

name: Schlumberger Foundation Faculty for the Future Fellowship
provider: Schlumberger Foundation (SLB corporate foundation)
fields: STEM (science, technology, engineering, mathematics) PhD or post-doctoral research
covers: Grant up to US$50,000 per year (PhD) or US$40,000 (post-doc), renewable, for tuition, living and research costs
eligibility: Woman and citizen of an eligible developing or emerging country where women are under-represented in STEM; no dual citizenship of a developed country; enrolled, admitted or applied to a PhD or post-doctoral program at a university abroad; excellent academic record; commitment to return home to teach/research; must demonstrate leadership and outreach
cambodia_note: Cambodia is on the Foundation's eligible country list; Cambodian women apply directly through the online portal
deadline_note: Applications open in September and close early November each year (7 November 2026, noon CST, for 2027 awards)

name: OWSD PhD Fellowships for Women Scientists from Science- and Technology-Lagging Countries
provider: Organization for Women in Science for the Developing World (OWSD) / Sida
fields: Natural, engineering and information technology sciences
eligibility: Woman scientist from one of the eligible least-developed/S&T-lagging countries; master's degree in a science field; full-time or sandwich PhD at a host institute in another developing country (Global South); maximum age 40 at application in past calls; must not reside in a developed country
cambodia_note: Cambodia (a UN Least Developed Country) is on OWSD's eligible country list; apply online. OWSD held no PhD call in 2025 and the next call date has not been announced, so check the site
deadline_note: Historically the call opened in October/November and closed in March/April; no call was issued in 2025 and the next call is not yet scheduled
language_req: English proficiency required by host institute

name: ASEAN-UK SAGE Women in STEM Scholarships (British Council)
provider: UK FCDO / UK Mission to ASEAN, delivered by the British Council
fields: STEM master's courses at partner UK universities (Cranfield University and University of Stirling)
eligibility: Women who are citizens and residents of an ASEAN member state (including Cambodia) or Timor-Leste; undergraduate degree qualifying for the chosen master's; demonstrated need for financial support; intend to return to home country; not previously funded by a UK government scholarship
cambodia_note: Cambodia is explicitly listed as eligible; apply directly to the partner UK university's scholarship page (see British Council Cambodia page for links)
deadline_note: Applications usually open in January/February and close in March/April each year for study starting the following September; the 2026-27 round has closed
language_req: IELTS 6.5 or equivalent (pre-sessional English support available)

name: Generation Google Scholarship (APAC)
provider: Google
fields: Computer science, computer engineering or closely related technical field
covers: One-off award of US$2,500 towards tuition/education expenses
invitation to a Google scholars retreat
invitation to a virtual Google scholars' retreat
eligibility: Students who identify as women (or who are otherwise under-represented in tech) enrolled full-time at a university in the Asia-Pacific region for the coming academic year; strong academic record; demonstrated leadership and passion for computer science
cambodia_note: Open to students at universities anywhere in Asia-Pacific, which includes Cambodia; apply directly online to Google
deadline_note: Usually opens around November/December and closes in January/February; check the page as dates shift year to year

name: Schwarzman Scholars
provider: Schwarzman Scholars / Tsinghua University (Stephen A. Schwarzman)
fields: One-year Master of Global Affairs at Schwarzman College, Tsinghua University, Beijing
eligibility: Undergraduate degree conferred by 1 August of enrollment year; aged 18 to under 29 on 1 August of enrollment year; any nationality; strong English proficiency (test scores unless studied in English for 2+ years); leadership potential
cambodia_note: Cambodians apply through the Global application (no embassy or government nomination); interviews are held regionally
deadline_note: Global application opens in April and closes in early-to-mid September each year (9 September 2026 for the 2027-28 cohort); the next cycle closes September 2027
language_req: TOEFL 100 / IELTS 7.0 or waiver for English-medium degree

name: Gates Cambridge Scholarship
provider: Gates Cambridge Trust (Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation endowment), University of Cambridge
fields: Any full-time postgraduate degree at the University of Cambridge (PhD, MPhil, one-year master's)
covers: discretionary academic development and family allowances
eligibility: Citizen of any country outside the UK; applying for a full-time postgraduate residential course at Cambridge; selected on academic excellence, reasons for choice of course, leadership and commitment to improving the lives of others
cambodia_note: Cambodians are in the international round; apply via the Cambridge Graduate Application Portal and tick the Gates Cambridge funding box
deadline_note: Opens early September; international applicants must apply by 4 December or the earlier course deadline; interviews in March

name: Global Rhodes Scholarships
provider: Rhodes Trust, University of Oxford
fields: Any full-time postgraduate degree at the University of Oxford
eligibility: Citizens of countries with no Rhodes constituency (Cambodia qualifies); aged 18 to 23 on 1 October of the year of application (up to 26 if first degree completed late); bachelor's degree with first-class or equivalent GPA; must be nominated by the university where the first degree was obtained; only two Global Scholarships per year
cambodia_note: Cambodia has no national Rhodes constituency, so Cambodians apply to the Global Rhodes Scholarships and must secure a nomination from their undergraduate university
deadline_note: Applications open in June; university nomination and application close around late July / early August each year for study the following October

name: Knight-Hennessy Scholars
provider: Stanford University (Knight-Hennessy Scholars program)
fields: Any full-time Stanford graduate degree (MA, MS, MBA, JD, MD, PhD, etc.)
eligibility: Citizens and residents of all countries; must earn first bachelor's degree in January 2020 or later (2027 cohort); must separately apply to and be admitted by a Stanford graduate program; no age or field restrictions
cambodia_note: Cambodians apply directly online; a separate Stanford graduate program application must also be submitted (by 1 December 2026 if the program deadline is later)
deadline_note: Application opens in early summer and closes in early October each year (6 October 2026, 1 pm Pacific, for the 2027 cohort)

name: Yenching Academy of Peking University Scholarship
provider: Peking University (Yenching Academy)
fields: Interdisciplinary Master's in China Studies (economics and management, history and archaeology, law and society, literature and culture, philosophy and religion, politics and international relations)
eligibility: Bachelor's degree obtained by August of enrollment year; typically aged under about 27 at enrollment; strong academic record; international applicants apply directly; English-language program (no Chinese required)
cambodia_note: Cambodians apply online directly to the Academy (international applicant track); interviews are conducted online or regionally
deadline_note: Applications for international candidates usually open in September and close in early December each year for enrollment the following September
language_req: English proficiency (TOEFL/IELTS unless degree taught in English)

name: Asian Development Bank - Japan Scholarship Program (ADB-JSP)
provider: Asian Development Bank, funded by the Government of Japan
fields: Economics, management, science and technology and other development-related fields at designated institutions in Japan, Australia, New Zealand, Singapore, Thailand, Hong Kong, India, Pakistan, Philippines, USA (Hawaii)
eligibility: National of an ADB borrowing member country eligible for Japanese ODA (Cambodia qualifies); bachelor's degree with excellent record; at least 2 years full-time professional experience after the degree; under 35 years old; proficient in English; not living/working outside home country; no dual citizenship of a developed country; must return home after study.
cambodia_note: Cambodians apply directly to one of the roughly 25 designated institutions (e.g. AIT Thailand, University of Tokyo, Hitotsubashi, Kyoto, Nagoya, Tsukuba, IUJ, Ritsumeikan APU, East-West Center, NUS, Melbourne, ANU, Auckland etc.) and indicate they wish to be considered for ADB-JSP; the institution endorses candidates to ADB. Living in Cambodia at time of application is required.
deadline_note: Deadlines set by each designated institution, typically about six months before the academic term (many fall between December and May); no direct application to ADB.
language_req: English proficiency required by the host university (typically IELTS 6.5 / TOEFL 80+)

name: Joint Japan/World Bank Graduate Scholarship Program (JJ/WBGSP)
provider: World Bank, funded by the Government of Japan
fields: Development-related master's programs at participating universities (preferred programs in the US, Europe, Japan, Australia, Africa and Asia; and partner programs in Japan)
eligibility: National of a World Bank member developing country (Cambodia is eligible); bachelor's degree earned at least 3 years before the application deadline; at least 3 years of paid development-related work experience; currently employed in paid development work; not a dual citizen of a developed country; not a World Bank Group staff member or relative; admitted unconditionally to a participating master's program
cambodia_note: Cambodians apply directly online during the two application windows after securing admission to a participating program; Cambodia is on the eligible developing-country list
deadline_note: Two windows each year: window 1 opens in January and closes late February; window 2 opens in March and closes about mid-May; partner-program (Japan) applications go through the universities
language_req: English proficiency required by the host university

name: Japan-IMF Scholarship Program for Asia (JISPA)
provider: International Monetary Fund, funded by the Government of Japan
fields: Macroeconomics, public finance, economics, public policy and related fields at partner universities (GRIPS, Hitotsubashi, University of Tokyo, International University of Japan)
eligibility: Citizen of an eligible Asian country including Cambodia; government official (central bank, ministry of finance, planning, statistics or similar) with strong potential for a policy-making career; bachelor's degree with strong academic record; under 40 preferred; strong English; must return to government service after study
cambodia_note: Cambodia is on the JISPA eligible country list; candidates are typically nominated through their government employer (e.g. National Bank of Cambodia, Ministry of Economy and Finance) and apply online to the IMF for the partnership track
deadline_note: Partnership-track applications usually open in October and close in early December each year for study starting the following October
language_req: TOEFL iBT or IELTS as required by partner universities

name: Obama Foundation Scholars Program
provider: Obama Foundation with Columbia University and the University of Chicago
fields: Columbia track: one-year non-degree leadership program at Columbia University; University of Chicago track: scholarship for final-year master's students at Harris (public policy), Crown Family School (social work) or Booth (business)
eligibility: Emerging leaders from any country with several years (typically 3-10) of demonstrated impact in civic or public work; commitment to return home to advance their work; for Chicago track, must have been admitted to and be in the final year of a qualifying UChicago master's program
cambodia_note: Cambodians may apply directly online; the Chicago track requires separate admission to a University of Chicago master's program
deadline_note: Columbia track usually opens around December and closes in January/February; Chicago track applications close in spring; 2026-27 cohorts have been selected, so next cycle is for 2027-28

name: Maurice R. Greenberg World Fellows Program (Yale World Fellows)
provider: Yale University (Jackson School of Global Affairs)
fields: Four-month mid-career global leadership fellowship (non-degree)
covers: travel to and from New Haven
eligibility: Mid-career professionals (typically 5-20 years of experience, usually aged early 30s to early 40s) with a record of leadership in any sector; fluent in English; citizens of any country outside the US (US citizens eligible only in limited cases); must be available for the full residential period (August to December)
cambodia_note: Open to Cambodian leaders; apply directly online to Yale, no nomination needed
deadline_note: Applications usually open in September/October and close in early December each year for the following August-December cohort

name: East-West Center Graduate Degree Fellowship
provider: East-West Center (US Congress-funded institution, Honolulu)
fields: Any master's or doctoral field offered by the University of Hawai'i at Manoa, with emphasis on Asia-Pacific issues
covers: tuition and fees (partial or full depending on funding)
eligibility: Citizens of Asia-Pacific countries (including Cambodia) and the US; must apply for and be admitted to a graduate program at the University of Hawai'i at Manoa; strong academic record; commitment to community building and Asia-Pacific engagement
cambodia_note: Cambodians are in the Asia-Pacific eligible group; apply online to the East-West Center and separately to the University of Hawai'i
deadline_note: Application opens in August and closes 1 December each year for study starting the following August
language_req: TOEFL/IELTS as required by the University of Hawai'i

name: UWC IB Diploma Scholarships via UWC Cambodia National Committee
provider: UWC International and the UWC Cambodia national committee (alumni volunteers), funded by UWC schools and donors
fields: Two-year International Baccalaureate Diploma Programme (pre-university) at one of 18 UWC schools, e.g. Li Po Chun UWC Hong Kong, Pearson College Canada, UWC Mahindra India, UWC ISAK Japan, UWC South East Asia Singapore
covers: full or partial need-based financial aid (over 80% of national-committee selected students receive support)
eligibility: Aged 16-19 at enrolment in August 2027; currently in the final two years of upper secondary school (grade 11 or 12); permanent residency in Cambodia; only one UWC application per year; selection weighs academic record, commitment to learning, intercultural understanding and resilience
cambodia_note: Apply online at apply.uwc.org choosing the UWC Cambodia national committee route; questions to selection@kh.uwc.org or the UWC Cambodia Facebook Messenger (fb.me/uwc.cambodia)
deadline_note: Applications for August 2027 entry close on 15 November 2026; the round usually opens around September each year
language_req: English-medium instruction; no formal test score required at application

name: Don Bosco Technical Schools Cambodia Scholarship Training
provider: Don Bosco Foundation of Cambodia (Salesians of Don Bosco)
fields: Technical trades: electricity, mechanics, automotive, welding, printing, IT and other vocational courses
eligibility: Disadvantaged Cambodian youth; two-year Higher Technical Diploma (associate-level) for grade-12 graduates; shorter C1, C2 and C3 certificate courses for those who have not completed grade 12
cambodia_note: Campuses in Phnom Penh, Sihanoukville, Kep, Battambang and Poipet; apply directly at the campus nearest you; about 500 graduates per year
deadline_note: Enrol before the Cambodian school year starts around October-November; contact each campus for exact dates

summary_en: Free technical training at Don Bosco campuses across Cambodia for disadvantaged youth, from short certificate courses to a two-year higher technical diploma.

name: Asia Kakehashi Project+ (Japan High School Scholarship)
provider: Government of Japan (MEXT) with AFS Intercultural Programs
fields: One academic year (or semester) at a Japanese high school with Japanese language study
eligibility: High school students aged 15-18 (birth-date window published per batch), currently in grades 9-11; for Cambodia at least 60% in all subjects in the latest exam and a 70% average over the past two years; good health; no Japanese required
cambodia_note: Cambodia is an eligible country; applications are announced by AFS/Embassy of Japan channels and submitted via an online form with ID, school results, vaccination record, family and house photos and parent income statement
deadline_note: Applications usually announced January-February with a deadline around March for departure in August-September; the project is scheduled to run through 2027

summary_en: Fully funded one academic year at a Japanese high school for students aged 15-18 from Asian countries including Cambodia, with airfare, housing and Japanese language training.
