name: JICA Scholarship Program – SDGs Global Leader Program (Cambodia)
provider: Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA)
fields: Development-related fields at Japanese universities including engineering, ICT, agriculture, health, environment, urban development, economics and public policy
eligibility: Cambodian national, usually under 40 (some cycles under 45), bachelor's degree, employed in a Cambodian government agency, public institution, university or private/civil organization relevant to development, with employer endorsement and commitment to return after graduation
cambodia_note: Announced and screened by the JICA Cambodia Office in Phnom Penh; candidates are shortlisted by JICA and must separately obtain admission from a partner Japanese university.
deadline_note: Call usually issued once a year (recent cycles around July–October) for enrolment in Japan the following autumn or spring; check the JICA Cambodia office announcement for the current cycle.
language_req: English (university may require TOEFL/IELTS); Japanese not required for English-taught programs

name: Ajinomoto Scholarship for ASEAN+ONE
provider: The Ajinomoto Foundation / Ajinomoto Co., Inc.
fields: Food science, nutrition, biosciences, agricultural and life sciences and related fields at designated Japanese universities (University of Tokyo, Kyoto, Nagoya, Ochanomizu, Kagawa Nutrition and others)
covers: monthly stipend (approx. JPY 150,000 as research student, JPY 180,000 as master's student)
entrance examination, admission and tuition fees
eligibility: National of one of the eligible ASEAN countries listed by the foundation (Cambodia has been listed in recent cycles; verify); under 35; bachelor's degree with strong grades; intends to enrol as a research student and then a master's course at a designated university; able to attend interview in home country; not already receiving another scholarship
cambodia_note: Application goes to the Ajinomoto Foundation / Ajinomoto Cambodia country contact and to the chosen Japanese university; typically one award per country per year.
deadline_note: Applications usually accepted in the first quarter of the year (roughly January–March) for enrolment the following year; confirm the current cycle on the foundation page.
language_req: English (TOEFL/IELTS or equivalent) or Japanese depending on the host laboratory

name: Rotary Yoneyama Scholarship for Overseas Applicants
provider: Rotary Yoneyama Memorial Foundation (Japan)
fields: any
covers: monthly stipend (approx. JPY 100,000 undergraduate; JPY 140,000 master's/doctoral)
eligibility: Non-Japanese national living outside Japan who has been accepted (or is applying) to a degree program at a Japanese university that participates in the overseas-applicant scheme; age limits generally under 45; good academic record; interest in Rotary exchange; cannot hold another major scholarship concurrently
cambodia_note: Cambodians apply through the participating Japanese university's international office (the university recommends candidates to the foundation); there is no embassy step in Phnom Penh.
deadline_note: Universities collect applications in autumn (around September–November) for April enrolment and in spring for October enrolment; exact dates vary by university.
language_req: Japanese or English as required by the host university

name: Honjo International Scholarship Foundation – Scholarship for Foreign Students in Japan
provider: Honjo International Scholarship Foundation
fields: any (STEM, business and social sciences all eligible)
covers: monthly stipend of about JPY 150,000–200,000 depending on program length
eligibility: Non-Japanese national planning to enrol full-time in a master's or doctoral program at a Japanese graduate school (or already enrolled); age under about 30 for master's and under 35 for doctoral at enrolment; not receiving another scholarship of comparable value; intends to contribute to home country
cambodia_note: Applied for online directly with the foundation from Cambodia or from Japan; no embassy or ministry nomination required.
deadline_note: Main application window is typically September to October each year for enrolment the following April; a smaller spring round has existed for October enrolment. Verify current cycle.
language_req: Japanese or English as required by the host graduate school

name: Otsuka Toshimi Scholarship
provider: Otsuka Toshimi Scholarship Foundation
fields: Medicine, pharmacy, nutrition/food science, physical education and business administration at Japanese universities
covers: annual scholarship of about JPY 1.4–2.0 million (paid monthly)
eligibility: Privately financed international student of any nationality already enrolled (or accepted) at a Japanese university or graduate school in an eligible field; good academic record; financial need; not receiving other major scholarships
cambodia_note: Cambodian students apply through the international student office of their Japanese university, which forwards the application to the foundation.
deadline_note: Applications usually collected by universities between February and mid-April each year for the academic year starting in April.
language_req: Japanese or English as required by the host university

name: JASSO Monbukagakusho Honors Scholarship for Privately-Financed International Students
provider: Japan Student Services Organization (JASSO), Government of Japan
fields: any
covers: monthly stipend (approx. JPY 48,000 for university/graduate students; JPY 30,000–40,000 for Japanese-language and preparatory courses)
eligibility: Privately financed international student of any nationality enrolled full-time at a Japanese university, graduate school, junior college, college of technology, specialized training college or Japanese-language institution; good academic performance; not receiving another scholarship above a set amount; also a reservation scheme for high scorers in the EJU exam
cambodia_note: Cambodians cannot apply directly: the Japanese school nominates enrolled students to JASSO. Candidates sitting the EJU (Examination for Japanese University Admission) can also apply for the reservation program through the exam.
deadline_note: Schools collect applications around April–May for the academic year; reservation program applies at EJU registration (June and November sittings).
language_req: none beyond the school's own admission requirements

name: Hitachi Global Foundation Scholarship (Hitachi Scholarship)
provider: The Hitachi Global Foundation
fields: Science and engineering fields (including environment, energy, ICT, materials, life sciences) for doctoral study or research at Japanese universities
eligibility: Young full-time faculty members or researchers at universities in the foundation's designated Southeast Asian countries (Cambodia has been listed in recent calls; verify), under about 35, master's degree, nominated by their home university, planning doctoral study or short research stay in Japan and return afterwards
cambodia_note: Nomination comes from the Cambodian home university (e.g. RUPP, ITC) to the foundation; individuals cannot apply without institutional endorsement.
deadline_note: Annual call usually opens in autumn with a deadline around November–December for study starting the following autumn.
language_req: English (TOEFL/IELTS) or Japanese as required by the host laboratory

name: Huawei Seeds for the Future – Cambodia
provider: Huawei Technologies (Cambodia) Co., Ltd. with the Ministry of Post and Telecommunications
fields: ICT: 5G, cloud, AI, cybersecurity, digital economy, plus leadership and cultural modules
covers: all program costs including travel and accommodation for the on-site component (when held in China)
eligibility: Cambodian citizen enrolled as an undergraduate (usually 2nd year or above) or master's student in ICT-related majors at a Cambodian university, generally aged 18–30, good academic standing and English; selected by written test and interview
cambodia_note: Applications are run locally by Huawei Cambodia together with the Ministry of Post and Telecommunications and partner universities; announcements appear on the Huawei Cambodia and MPTC Facebook pages.
deadline_note: Held once a year; Cambodian recruitment usually runs around May–August with the program in the second half of the year. Verify current cycle.
language_req: English (working proficiency; no fixed test score)

name: GitHub Student Developer Pack
provider: GitHub Education (Microsoft)
fields: Software development and computing (tools, cloud credits, courses)
covers: cloud and hosting credits from partner companies
free courses and certifications from partners
eligibility: Student aged 13+ enrolled in a degree- or diploma-granting course at an accredited institution anywhere in the world; must verify with school email, student ID or enrolment document
cambodia_note: Cambodian students verify directly on the GitHub Education site; a school-issued document is accepted if the university has no student email domain.
deadline_note: Rolling; apply any time and renew verification annually.

name: Coursera Financial Aid
provider: Coursera
fields: any (individual courses, specializations and professional certificates from partner universities and companies)
covers: waived or reduced course fee for the specific course applied for
access to graded assignments and certificate
eligibility: Any learner worldwide who cannot afford the fee; separate application per course with income statement and short essays; not available for degrees or some MasterTrack programs
cambodia_note: Cambodians apply from the course page ('Financial aid available'); no local partner needed.
deadline_note: Rolling; decisions usually take up to 15 days after applying.

name: edX Financial Assistance
provider: edX (2U)
fields: any (verified-track courses from partner universities)
covers: up to 90% discount on the verified certificate fee for eligible courses
eligibility: Learners of any country who demonstrate financial need; per-course application with a short statement; excludes some programs (e.g. MicroMasters, professional certificates, degrees) and learners in sanctioned countries
cambodia_note: Cambodians apply online through the edX learner dashboard for each course; no local step.
deadline_note: Rolling; apply before the course's upgrade deadline.

name: Harvard College Need-Based Financial Aid (need-blind for international students)
provider: Harvard College (Harvard University)
fields: any
covers: books and personal expenses (need-based, grant only, no loans)
eligibility: Admitted first-year undergraduates of any nationality; aid is 100% need-based (no merit). Families earning under USD 100,000 pay nothing; families up to USD 200,000 get at least full tuition covered. Admission is need-blind for foreign citizens.
cambodia_note: Cambodian applicants apply directly online through the Common Application/Coalition; financial aid is awarded on exactly the same basis as for US students. No embassy or ministry involvement; submit CSS Profile (Harvard code 3434) plus translated parent income documents.
deadline_note: Applications open in August; Restrictive Early Action deadline 1 November, Regular Decision deadline early January each year; CSS Profile due at the same time as the admission application.
language_req: English; TOEFL/IELTS/Duolingo not required but may be submitted

name: MIT Need-Based Financial Aid for International Undergraduates (need-blind, full need)
provider: Massachusetts Institute of Technology
fields: any (MIT undergraduate programs, STEM-focused)
covers: books and personal expenses (need-based MIT Scholarship)
eligibility: Admitted undergraduates of any citizenship; MIT is need-blind and meets 100% of demonstrated financial need for all four years. Aid amount depends on family finances via CSS Profile and parental income documents.
cambodia_note: Cambodian nationals apply directly through the MIT online application; international students use the same aid process as domestic students (CSS Profile plus parent income documentation). No government nomination.
deadline_note: Application opens in August; Early Action deadline 1 November, Regular Action deadline early January; CSS Profile due mid-February for aid.
language_req: English; TOEFL/IELTS/Duolingo/Cambridge optional but recommended for non-native speakers

name: Yale College Need-Based Financial Aid for International Students (need-blind)
provider: Yale University
fields: any
covers: travel to and from campus twice a year
books and personal expenses (grant-based, no loans)
eligibility: Admitted Yale College students of any citizenship; awards are 100% need-based and meet full demonstrated need without loans. Awards account for the economic difference between the US and the student's home country.
cambodia_note: Cambodian students apply directly online (Common App/Coalition/QuestBridge) and submit the CSS Profile; financial need does not affect admission for any applicant anywhere in the world.
deadline_note: Applications open in August; Single-Choice Early Action deadline 1 November, Regular Decision deadline early January each year.
language_req: English; TOEFL/IELTS/Duolingo recommended if English is not the language of instruction

name: Princeton University Need-Based Financial Aid for International Students (need-blind)
provider: Princeton University
fields: any
covers: books and personal expenses (100% grant, no loans)
eligibility: Admitted undergraduates of any nationality; Princeton is need-blind for all applicants including international students and meets 100% of demonstrated need with grants. Entirely need-based, no academic or athletic merit scholarships.
cambodia_note: Cambodian applicants apply directly online; the same aid application (Princeton Financial Aid Application) and full-need policy apply to international students. No embassy or ministry process.
deadline_note: Applications open in August; Single-Choice Early Action deadline 1 November, Regular Decision deadline 1 January each year.
language_req: English; TOEFL/IELTS/PTE required unless English is the primary language of instruction

name: Amherst College Need-Based Financial Aid for International Students (need-blind)
provider: Amherst College
fields: any (liberal arts)
covers: travel allowance (scholarships and grants; no loans packaged)
eligibility: Admitted international students who apply for need-based aid; Amherst is need-blind for international applicants and meets 100% of calculated need. Need is met first with a work-study expectation and the rest by scholarship.
cambodia_note: Cambodian nationals apply directly via the Common Application and submit the CSS Profile with parent income documents; treated identically to domestic applicants for aid.
deadline_note: Applications open in August; Early Decision deadline 1 November (ED II around 1 January), Regular Decision deadline early January each year.
language_req: English; TOEFL/IELTS/Duolingo expected for non-native English speakers

name: Dartmouth College Universal Need-Blind Financial Aid for International Students
provider: Dartmouth College
fields: any
covers: books and personal expenses (full-tuition scholarship without loans for family income under USD 125,000; zero parent contribution under USD 65,000)
eligibility: Admitted undergraduates of any citizenship; need-blind admission for all international applicants since the Class of 2026 and 100% of demonstrated need met. Aid is need-based only.
cambodia_note: Cambodian students apply directly through the Common Application and submit the CSS Profile and income documents; no nomination or embassy step.
deadline_note: Applications open in August; Early Decision deadline 1 November, Regular Decision deadline early January each year.
language_req: English; TOEFL/IELTS/Duolingo recommended for non-native speakers

name: Bowdoin College Need-Blind Admission and Full-Need Aid for International Students
provider: Bowdoin College
fields: any (liberal arts)
covers: books and personal expenses (grants only, no loans)
eligibility: First-year applicants of any citizenship; need-blind admission and 100% of calculated need met without loans. Not available to international transfer students.
cambodia_note: Cambodian applicants apply directly via the Common Application and file the CSS Profile; family ability to pay is not considered in admission.
deadline_note: Applications open in August; Early Decision I deadline 15 November, Early Decision II and Regular Decision deadline early January each year.
language_req: English; TOEFL/IELTS/Duolingo recommended for non-native speakers

name: Brown University Need-Blind Financial Aid for International Undergraduates
provider: Brown University
fields: any
covers: books and personal expenses (100% of demonstrated need met, no loans)
eligibility: First-year international applicants (need-blind from the Class of 2029, entering fall 2025, onward); aid is need-based and meets 100% of demonstrated need for all admitted students.
cambodia_note: Cambodian students apply directly via the Common Application and submit the CSS Profile with parental income documents; no nomination required.
deadline_note: Applications open in August; Early Decision deadline 1 November, Regular Decision deadline early January each year.
language_req: English; TOEFL/IELTS/Duolingo recommended for non-native speakers

name: APU Tuition Reduction Scholarship for International Students
provider: Ritsumeikan Asia Pacific University (with MEXT and corporate/individual donors)
fields: any APU program (Asia Pacific Studies, International Management, Sustainability and Tourism; graduate programs)
covers: tuition reduction of 30%, 50%, 65%, 80% or 100% for the standard period until graduation
eligibility: International applicants who will hold a Japanese 'Student' residence status before enrolling; assessed on financial need, application documents, online assessment and recorded video interview. Applying earlier in each enrollment period improves chances.
cambodia_note: Cambodian nationals apply directly through the APU online application and tick the scholarship request in the same application; no embassy or ministry step. APU has a large Southeast Asian student body.
deadline_note: Several application periods each year for April and September enrollment (2027 enrollment applications running through 2026-27); scholarship is requested at the time of the admission application and early applicants have a greater chance.
language_req: English-basis: TOEFL iBT/IELTS or equivalent; Japanese-basis: JLPT N2 or higher

name: KAIST International Undergraduate Scholarship (KAIST Scholarship)
provider: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology (KAIST)
fields: STEM (all KAIST undergraduate majors; non-declared major system in first year)
covers: full tuition for up to 8 semesters
eligibility: International high-school graduates (or expected graduates) who are not Korean citizens and hold no Korean dual citizenship; strong mathematics and science record; scholarship selected during admission review when 'KAIST Scholarship' is ticked on the Statement of Financial Resources.
cambodia_note: Cambodian students apply online directly to KAIST (apply.kaist.ac.kr) for the Fall intake only; no government nomination. Scholarship results are announced with admission results.
deadline_note: Fall 2027 intake: Early Admissions closes 22 October 2026 (recommendations by 29 October); Regular Admissions opens 10 November 2026 and closes 14 January 2027 (recommendations by 21 January 2027).
language_req: English proficiency (TOEFL/IELTS/TOEIC etc.) recommended; instruction in English

name: Yonsei University Underwood International College (UIC) Admissions Scholarship
provider: Yonsei University, Underwood International College
fields: any UIC major (humanities, social sciences, sciences, engineering, techno-art; taught in English)
covers: full tuition for 4 years (admissions scholarship); need-based full, half or one-third tuition awards for enrolled students
eligibility: Newly admitted international students at UIC are automatically considered; selection based on admission evaluation. Need-based and merit-based awards continue for enrolled students based on GPA and financial circumstances.
cambodia_note: Cambodian nationals apply through the Yonsei international admissions portal for UIC; scholarship consideration is automatic with the admission application.
deadline_note: Two international admission rounds each year: applications for Spring entry close around September-October and for Fall entry around March-May; check UIC admissions page for exact dates.

name: Korea University International Admission Scholarships (Global Leader Scholarship A/B)
provider: Korea University, Office of International Affairs
fields: any Korea University undergraduate major
covers: partial to full tuition waiver based on admission evaluation
eligibility: International undergraduate applicants (both parents non-Korean) admitted through the international admission track; scholarships are awarded from the application documents, no separate application. Results announced with admission results.
cambodia_note: Cambodian nationals apply online via the Korea University OIA international admission portal; no nomination required.
deadline_note: Freshman admissions for Fall intake usually accept applications around February-April and for Spring intake around September-October; see the current Application Guide.
language_req: English (TOEFL/IELTS) or Korean (TOPIK) depending on program

name: SMU ASEAN Undergraduate Scholarship
provider: Singapore Management University
fields: any SMU undergraduate degree (business, economics, accountancy, law, computing, social sciences)
covers: 100% of subsidised tuition fees after MOE Tuition Grant
eligibility: Citizens of ASEAN member countries excluding Singapore (Cambodia is explicitly listed); awarded on merit; recipients must accept the MOE Tuition Grant with 3-year work bond in Singapore; cannot hold other scholarships concurrently without approval.
cambodia_note: Cambodia is named among eligible countries; Cambodian applicants apply for SMU admission online and are considered for the scholarship on the strength of their application.
deadline_note: SMU international applications typically open in October and close around February-March for the August intake.

name: HKU Entrance Scholarships for International Students
provider: The University of Hong Kong
fields: any HKU full-time undergraduate program
covers: accommodation and general living allowance (top awards)
eligibility: Outstanding non-local applicants with international qualifications (IB, A-levels, SAT/AP, national exams) admitted to full-time undergraduate degrees; merit-based; automatically considered on submission of the admission application, no separate scholarship application.
cambodia_note: Cambodian students apply directly through HKU's online international admissions; scholarship results are announced with the admission offer.
deadline_note: International applications open in September; main round deadline typically in early-mid January for September entry, with later rounds accepted until the summer.

name: HKUST Academic Admissions Scholarships and Global Learners Scholarship
provider: The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology
fields: any HKUST undergraduate program
covers: up to HKD 60,000 allowance per year (top awards), renewable
eligibility: All undergraduate applicants with international qualifications are automatically considered on academic merit and non-academic achievements; the Global Learners Scholarship targets applicants from underrepresented nationalities. No separate application.
cambodia_note: Cambodian applicants apply online through HKUST Undergraduate Admissions; as an underrepresented nationality they are automatically considered for the Global Learners Scholarship as well as academic scholarships.
deadline_note: Applications open in September; early round deadline around mid-November and main round around early January for September entry.

name: CUHK Admission Scholarships for International Students
provider: The Chinese University of Hong Kong
fields: any CUHK full-time undergraduate program
covers: allowance up to HKD 66,000 per year (selected awards), renewable
one-off awards HKD 50,000-214,000 for non-academic excellence
eligibility: Local and non-local new undergraduates with excellent academic or non-academic performance; no application needed, CUHK identifies qualified admitted students automatically.
cambodia_note: Cambodian students apply through CUHK international undergraduate admissions online and are automatically considered for admission scholarships.
deadline_note: International applications open in September/October; early round deadline typically early January, with later rounds through the spring for September entry.

name: Mahidol Postgraduate Scholarships for International Students
provider: Mahidol University, Faculty of Graduate Studies
fields: any master's or doctoral program at Mahidol (some medical programs excluded)
covers: additional expenses/allowance as specified in the annual announcement
eligibility: International students eligible for enrollment in a Mahidol master's or doctoral program in the relevant academic year; selection by academic merit; must meet program English requirements.
cambodia_note: Cambodian students apply for admission to a Mahidol graduate program and submit the scholarship application through the Faculty of Graduate Studies; Cambodian nationals are also specifically eligible for the CMB Foundation Mekong Region postgraduate scholarship at Mahidol.
deadline_note: Announced annually (2026 round published for academic year 2026); applications typically accepted in the first half of the year for August entry.

name: CMB Foundation Mahidol Postgraduate Scholarship for Mekong Region Scholars
provider: China Medical Board (CMB) Foundation and Mahidol University
fields: postgraduate programs at Mahidol University (health and related fields)
eligibility: Nationals of Cambodia, Lao PDR, Myanmar and Vietnam admitted to a Mahidol postgraduate program; academic merit and commitment to return to contribute in home country.
cambodia_note: Cambodia is explicitly named as an eligible country; apply for admission to Mahidol and then for the CMB Mekong Region scholarship through the Faculty of Graduate Studies.
deadline_note: Announced through the Faculty of Graduate Studies each year; typically applications in the first half of the year for August entry.

name: Asian University for Women Need-Based Scholarships
provider: Asian University for Women (AUW), Chattogram
fields: liberal arts and sciences (undergraduate; plus pre-undergraduate Pathways/Access programs)
covers: international travel (full scholarship); partial scholarships also offered
eligibility: Women from Asia (primarily South, Southeast, West Asia and Middle East) who have completed 10+2 secondary education with roughly 60% average including English and mathematics; need-blind admission; demonstrated leadership and commitment to social change; aid based on demonstrated financial need.
cambodia_note: Cambodian women apply online directly to AUW; Cambodia is within the Southeast Asia recruitment region and AUW has enrolled Cambodian students. Scholarship application is part of the admission process.
deadline_note: Applications for the following academic year generally open around October-November and close around March-May; rolling review.
language_req: English (minimum 60% in English exam; AUW's own assessment; no IELTS required)

name: KAUST Fellowship
provider: King Abdullah University of Science and Technology (KAUST)
fields: STEM (17 disciplines across engineering, physical, biological, computer and environmental sciences)
eligibility: Bachelor's degree (for MS) or relevant master's (for PhD) in a STEM field with strong GPA; GRE optional; English proficiency (TOEFL iBT 79 / IELTS 6.5) unless exempt; all admitted students automatically receive the fellowship (no separate application).
cambodia_note: Cambodian nationals apply directly through the KAUST online application; no nomination or embassy process; the fellowship is automatic on admission.
deadline_note: Applications for 2027 entry open mid-August 2026; Spring 2027 (PhD only) and Fall 2027 (MS, MS/PhD, PhD) deadlines are published on the admission timeline (Fall deadlines usually fall between January and March).
language_req: TOEFL iBT 79 or IELTS 6.5 (waived for graduates of English-medium universities in listed countries)

name: Lester B. Pearson International Student Scholarship
provider: University of Toronto
fields: any U of T undergraduate program
covers: full residence support for four years
eligibility: International students (non-Canadian, requiring a study permit) in their final year of secondary school or graduated no earlier than June 2026; must be nominated by their school; must begin U of T studies in September 2027; about 37 awards per year based on academic excellence, creativity and leadership.
cambodia_note: Cambodian students must be nominated by their Cambodian (or international) secondary school, which registers with U of T; then apply for admission and complete the Pearson application. No embassy process.
deadline_note: Nomination portal opens 6 July 2026; school nomination deadline 9 October 2026; U of T admission application deadline 16 October 2026; Pearson scholarship application deadline 6 November 2026.
language_req: English (IELTS 6.5 / TOEFL iBT 100 or U of T-recognised English-medium schooling)

name: Bocconi4Access to Education Need-Based Scholarships and Tuition Waivers for International Students
provider: Bocconi University (Università Bocconi), Milan
fields: economics, management, finance, data science, political science, law
covers: full or partial tuition waiver based on family economic need
some awards include accommodation and a living allowance (Bocconi Scholarship for International Students)
eligibility: International candidates admitted to the first year of a Bachelor/Law or Master of Science program for a.y. 2027-28 who submit the Bocconi4Access to Education application with family income and asset documentation; merit is assessed from the admission application.
cambodia_note: Cambodian applicants apply online for Bocconi admission and submit the Bocconi4Access application in the same portal; no embassy involvement.
deadline_note: Bachelor: early session applications close in the autumn and further sessions run until early spring 2027, with the funding request submitted alongside the admission application; Master: four selection rounds between September 2026 and April 2027, most scholarships allocated in earlier rounds.
language_req: English (IELTS/TOEFL/Cambridge; SAT/ACT or Bocconi test for bachelor)

name: University of Bologna International Talents Scholarship and Unibo Action 2 Study Grants
provider: Alma Mater Studiorum - Università di Bologna
fields: any (calls specify eligible degree programmes; International Talents targets second-cycle master's)
covers: study grant (EUR 6,500 per year for 2 years for International Talents; EUR 11,000 gross under Unibo Action 2)
eligibility: International students (admission qualification obtained outside the Italian system) matriculating in an eligible Bologna degree programme; merit-based on admission test scores or academic record; must not already hold an Italian degree.
cambodia_note: Cambodian students apply through the annual call on bandi.unibo.it while applying for admission; no embassy step. Contact internationaldesk@unibo.it for the current call.
deadline_note: Calls are usually published around January-February with deadlines around March-May for enrolment the following September.
language_req: English B2 (IELTS 6.0 or equivalent) for English-taught programmes; Italian B2 for Italian-taught programmes

name: ANU Chancellor's International Scholarship
provider: The Australian National University
fields: any ANU undergraduate or postgraduate coursework program
covers: 25% or 50% tuition fee reduction for the duration of the program
eligibility: International students applying for admission to ANU; automatically assessed across 9 citizenship-based categories (at least one open to students from anywhere in the world); awarded on academic merit; no separate application.
cambodia_note: Cambodian applicants apply online for ANU admission and are automatically assessed for the highest-value category they are eligible for.
deadline_note: Automatic with admission; ANU accepts international applications year-round for February and July intakes (apply several months before the intake).

name: Melbourne Research Scholarship (Graduate Research Scholarships)
provider: The University of Melbourne
fields: any graduate research (Masters by Research or PhD)
covers: full tuition fee offset (2 years MRes / 4 years PhD)
living allowance AUD 39,500 per year (2026 rate)
relocation grant AUD 3,000 for overseas students
eligibility: International applicants to a Masters by Research or doctoral degree with excellent academic results and research potential; automatically considered when applying for admission; over 300 awards per year to international candidates.
cambodia_note: Cambodian applicants submit a graduate research application online (with supervisor agreement) and are automatically considered; no separate scholarship form.
deadline_note: Applications accepted year-round; international candidates should apply by 31 October for the following year's main scholarship round (later rounds in the first half of the year).
language_req: English (IELTS 6.5 with no band below 6.0 or TOEFL iBT 79, program-dependent)
